[[Angel]] | None | N/A |} ===Magic === Ninjas cannot use staves or books, and so primarily use Asura or Bazerald as these daggers raise their MATK. Of the two, Bazerald is the superior choice but may be too expensive for many. Asura [3] with Drops cards represents the next best thing in a magic ninja's arsenal. In terms of other equipment, magic ninja tend to focus on stacking INT to reach the highest MATK bonus possible. While still important, DEX is of lesser priority for ninja compared to other spell casters as their repertoire of fast casting spells means that DEX gets less value when compared to a job like [[Wizard]]. A Punk carded Hood [1] is a very cheap tool that can help with mobbing, as the [[Quagmire]] 1 effect can trigger even if damage isn't directly taken (i.e., [[Cicada Skin Shed]] is triggered), and can help with mobbing faster groups of enemies with [[Blaze Shield]]. Crown [0] and unslotted Earrings are good first investments for new players providing they haven't already obtained a Vitata and Creamy carded accessory (which can very easily be hunted by magic ninja). {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" | Example Equipment | Some example budget/starter equipment for Magic Ninja: *Head: Crown [0]/Tiara [0], Geek Glasses, Mr. Scream/Smile *Weapon: Asura [2] *Shield: Arm Guard [0] *Body: Thief Clothes [0] *Garment: Hood [1] (Punk card) *Boots: Shoes [0] *Accessories: Earring [0], Glove [0], Clip [1] (Creamy card, Vitata card) *Pet: Baby Desert Wolf Some example higher-end equipment for Magic Ninja: *Head: Fricca's Circlet, Apple of Archer, Crown [0]/Tiara [0], Crown of Mistress *Weapon: Bazerald, Asura [3] (Drops card x 3) *Shield: Guard [1] (Any racial card), Advanced Arm Guard [1] (Any racial card, Horn card) *Body: Guardian's Robes [1]/Sacred Saint's Robes [1]/Thief Clothes [1] (Baby Desert Wolf Card, any elemental armor card like Bathory), Ninja Suit *Garment: Muffler/Heavenly Maiden's Robe [1] (Raydric card, Noxious card, Punk Card) *Boots: Shoes [1] (Kalec card, Living Magma card) *Accessories: Earring [1] (Zerom card), Glove [1] (Zerom card), Earring [0], Shinobi Sash *Pet: Munak, Dokebi, Isis, Kalec, Baby Desert Wolf |} === Throwing (AGI) === Throwing (AGI) Ninjas generally use properly carded Main Gauche [4] to maximize their [[Haze Slasher]] and [[Shadow Slash]] damage. This usually means specific weapons for each area (e.g., 2x peco peco egg + 2x drainliar Main Gauche [4] for killing Siroma) or more generalized weapons (e.g., 4x Drainliar Main Gauche [4]). At least as far as carded Main gauche [4]s are concerned, these ninja share their weapons of choice with DD [[Assassin]]s and [[Shield Boomerang]] [[Crusader]]s. Similar to other melee builds, these ninja aim for ATK-boosting equipment and stack STR to reach the highest (multiple of 10) bonus possible. Flee-boosting cards like whisper or nine tails are also used. The Ninja Suit + Shinobi Sash combo represents a valuable tool for farming easier enemies or reducing downtime. Kamaitachi [0] are a great purchase for new ninja, as it is a higher attack, considerably cheaper elemental dagger compared to blacksmith-made elemental damascus (which are another option). A Poring Dagger is a very affordable weapon with a +20% [[Formless]] damage boost and high weapon ATK. Khukri is another cheap weapon option that boasts a useful effect ([[Curse]] on hit) with high attack. A Main Gauche [4] with 4 Goblin cards represents a good first carded weapon to pursue, as it's relatively cheap, easy to farm and is a solid option for many good targets like Spring Rabbits, Minorous and Ninetails. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" | Example Equipment | Some example budget/starter equipment for Throwing (AGI) Ninja: *Head: Sakkat, Momoe's Hairband, Mr. Scream/Smile, Geek Glasses *Weapon: Poring Dagger, Kamaitachi, Khukri, VVS elemental damascus, Main Gauche [4] (Goblin card x 4) *Shield: Arm Guard [0] *Body: Pantie *Garment: Undershirt *Boots: Shoes [0], Sandals [1] (Male Thief Bug card) *Accessories: Matyr's Leash, Brooch [0], Ring [0] *Pet: Picky, Drops Some example higher-end equipment for Throwing (AGI) Ninja: *Head: Marionette Doll [1] (Deviruchi card, Cramp card), Magni's Cap, Momoe's Hairband, Hot-Blooded Headband, Ghost Bandana, Crown of Mistress, Evil/Angel Wing Ears, Aggyu Mask, Scouting Scarf *Weapon: Main Gauche [4] (2x2x race/element card, or 4x race/element card) *Shield: Guard [1] (Any racial card), Advanced Arm Guard [1] (Any racial card, Horn card) *Body: Thief Clothes [1] or any slotted armor (Porcellio card), Ninja Suit *Garment: Muffler/Heavenly Maiden's Robe [1] (Giant Whisper card, Whisper card), +8 Hood [1] (Nine Tails card) *Boots: Shoes [1] (Firelock Soldier card, Male Thief Bug card, Sohee Card, Matyr Card), +8 Sandals [1] (Spectring card), Fricco's Shoes *Accessories: Ring [1]/Brooch [1] (Mantis, Tarou, Kukre, Spring Rabbit, Snowier), Shinobi Sash *Pet: Orc Warrior, Yser, Earth Petite, Picky |} === Throwing (DEX) === Throwing (DEX) Ninjas primarily use properly carded Huuma Calm Mind [2]s to maximize their [[Throw Huuma Shuriken]] damage. This means specific weapons for each area (e.g., a 2x Peco Peco Egg Huuma Calm Mind [2] for killing Stings). Some DEX throwers opt to use Huuma Giant Wheel Shuriken [4] as their weapons of choice so that they can use the same weapon for both [[Shadow Slash]] and [[Throw Huuma Shuriken]]. A Huuma Blaze Shuriken [0] can also be used for its innate [[Fire]] property, high base ATK and high availability. Like their AGI counterparts, Throwing (DEX) ninja should aim to maximize +ATK-boosting equipment and reach as high as possible a strength bonus as they can. Unlike AGI ninjas however, they do not pursue flee-boosting cards like Nine Tails or Whisper. Aside from magic builds, DEX thrower ninja are one of the somewhat cheaper builds and a reasonable choice for a new player who wants to play ninja. The bare minimum for this build to function reasonably well (at level 75+ when you roughly start using [[Throw Huuma Shuriken]]) is to acquire at least one Huuma Calm Mind [2]. These weapons are not expensive, but rarely sold. They drop off Kapha in Amatsu Field 01 at a relatively high rate. 2 Goblin cards or 2 Peco Peco Egg cards are good first choices for carding these weapons, and are relatively easy to farm. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" | Example Equipment | Some example budget/starter equipment for Throwing (DEX) Ninja: *Head: Sakkat, Kitsune's Mask, Mr. Scream/Smile, Geek Glasses *Weapon: Huuma Calm Mind [2] (Peco Peco Egg card x2, Goblin card x2), Poring Dagger, Kamaitachi, Khukri, VVS elemental damascus *Shield: Arm Guard [0] *Body: Thief Clothes [0] *Garment: Hood [1] (Punk card) *Boots: Shoes [0] *Accessories: Ring [0], Glove [0] *Pet: Picky Some example higher-end equipment for Throwing (DEX) Ninja: *Head: Marionette Doll [1] (Deviruchi card, Cramp card), Magni's Cap, Hot-Blooded Headband, Crown of Mistress, Evil/Angel Wing Ears, Aggyu Mask *Weapon: Huuma Calm Mind [2] (2x race or clement card), Huuma Giant Wheel Shuriken [4] (2x2x or 4x race/element cards, for [[Shadow Slash]]) Main Gauche [4] (2x2x or 4x race/element cards, for [[Shadow Slash]] and early-mid leveling with [[Throw Kunai]]) *Shield: N/A *Body: Sacred Saint's Robes [1]/Thief Clothes [1] (Porcellio card), Ninja Suit *Garment: Muffler/Heavenly Maiden's Robe [1] (Raydric card, Noxious card) *Boots: Shoes [1] (Firelock Soldier card, Sohee Card) *Accessories: Ring [1] (Mantis, Tarou), Glove [1] (Zerom card), Shinobi Sash *Pet: Orc Warrior, Picky |} === Shadow Slash Critical === Shadow Slash Crit ninja generally use Huuma Giant Wheel Shuriken [4] as their primary weapon as huuma avoid size penalties. Consider whether one or more race crit % card like Cruiser card or Assaulter card is going to be needed for your build to reach 50% crit (i.e., 100% crit with [[Shadow's Within]] [[Shadow Slash]]) when deciding on weapons (See: [[#Ninja#Cards_(+%_Crit)]]). To reach this value, Shadow Slash ninja use different combinations of LUK, weapon cards and equipment. The following are ''example'' combinations and are by no means definitive, serving only as a reference. *12% CRIT from gear (Goddess of Cursed Fortune Brooch, Yoyo Pet, Ruby Pumps) + 14% CRIT from weapon cards + 71 LUK *15% CRIT from gear (Goddess of Cursed Fortune Brooch, Yoyo Pet, Ruby Pumps) + 7% CRIT from weapon cards + 84 LUK *17% CRIT from gear (+9 Green Maiden Hood [1], Ring of the Claw, Yoyo Pet, Ruby Pumps) + 7% CRIT from weapon cards + 78 LUK ''(LUK refers to base values)'' One unusual thing that shadow slash ninja share in common with SB [[Assassin]]s and MvP Rifle [[Gunslinger]]s is their potential use of the Goddess of Cursed Fortune Brooch accessories. These three builds are the only CRIT-based characters that generally use these accessories, as being skill-based builds their rate of attacks is very slow, and the probability of being [[Curse]]d by the accessory much lower. Regardless, any ninja wanting to make use of this accessory should carry some Holy Water with them, just in case. As mentioned in the [[Ninja#Shadow_Slash_Critical]] section, it isn't recommended to make these type of ninja without already being an established player with the necessary equipment. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+ class="nowrap" | Example Equipment | Some example equipment for Shadow Slash Critical Ninjas: *Head: Marionette Doll [1] (Deviruchi card, Cramp card), Magni's Cap, Momoe's Hairband, Hot-Blooded Headband, Evil/Angel Wing Ears, Aggyu Mask *Weapon: Huuma Giant Wheel Shuriken [4] (Combination of crit%race and race cards, see [[Ninja#Cards_(+%_Crit)]]), Main Gauche [4] (2x2x or 4x race/element cards, for early-mid leveling with [[Throw Kunai]]), Gladius [3] (3x race or element cards, for early-mid leveling with [[Throw Kunai]]) *Shield: None *Body: Thief Clothes [1] or any slotted armor (Porcellio card) *Garment: Muffler/Heavenly Maiden's Robe [1] (Giant Whisper card, Raydric Card), +8/9 Hood [1] (Green Maiden aka CHUNG-E card) *Boots: Ruby Pumps, Crystal Pumps, Shoes [1] (Firelock Soldier Card, Sohee Card) *Accessories: Ring [1]/Rosary [1] (Mantis, Tarou, Kobold), Ring of the Claw *Pet: Yoyo, Lunatic |} === Killing Stroke === Because weapon damage is irrelevant (but [[Killing Stroke]] benefits from +% cards), a properly carded Main Gauche [4] is typically used (Usually 2x2x race/element for monsters, or 2x2x race/size for PvP/WoE). These Ninja use an unusual assortment of equipment because they don't care about the ATK stat, but still benefit greatly from STR. The formula for [[Killing Stroke]] is "(STR*40) + (HP*80%)", so their equipment aims to maximize STR and maxHP ''without'' the typical focus of hitting multiples of 10 for STR. [[Ninja Training]] ticks every 5 seconds while standing/sitting. ''Standing'' only means when the ninja isn't actively walking, i.e., movement produced from skills like [[Shadow Jump]], [[Shadow Slash]] and [[Cicada Skin Shed]] does not interrupt ticks from this skill, nor does using fly wings or teleport. That means the best way to maximize SP recovery from the passive skill is try and walk as little as possible. Leveling on a map by using fly wings or teleport is especially advantageous for ninja. Try to avoid little bits of movement between skills like [[Throw Kunai]] or [[Throw Shuriken]] if you're in the habit of staggering movement on other classes. To further aid in SP management, ninja and [[Thief]] classes can use the Ninja Suit (Shinobi 0.03% drop) + Shinobi Sash (Shinobi 0.03% drop, also obtained from old blue box/old purple box by low chance) combo to reduce SP consumption by 20%. It's also typical for non-magic ninja classes to also get at least 21 base INT for their final build. 21 base INT adds up to 36 total with job bonuses + [[Ninja Aura]], which is a multiple of 6 ''and'' brings MaxSP to ~700 for the purposes of increasing SP regen (every 100 MaxSP = 1 extra regen). Finally, when killing targets with [[Shadow's Within]] [[Shadow Slash]], consider that all SP regeneration including [[Ninja Training]] ticks is '''halted''' when in the [[Hiding]] status from something like [[Shadow Jump]]. waiting ~1 second after each [[Shadow Slash]] is best practice for accommodating the 3 second delay from [[Shadow's Within]]. ===Sight Shadow Jump=== Normally the [[Shadow Jump]] skill enters the ninja into [[Hiding]] status upon use. However, if the [[Sight]] spell is active (from any accessory with a Horong Card) then the [[Hiding]] status is immediately cancelled, allowing the ninja to repeatedly teleport around with [[Shadow Jump]]. Aside from just rapid movement, this is useful for mobbing, leading enemies into [[Blaze Shield]] cells (especially fast enemies), and for hopping over enemies in narrow spaces without getting hit. [[File:SightJump_Demonstration4.gif|center|SightJump_Demonstration4.gif]] ===Blaze Shield and Mobbing=== [[Blaze Shield]] functions differently depending on whether multiple targets are hit by it. When two or more enemies are inside the spell's area, the skill changes to where any target hit produces a 3x3 AoE (50% MATK) at 3x the number of hits consumed per ember. Put another way, if one enemy inside a lvl 10 Blaze Shield would be hit 9 times per ember, 5 enemies inside a lvl 10 Blaze Shield would get hit 3 times per ember.
[[File:BSDemo3.gif|BSDemo3.gif]] [[File:BSD21.gif|BSD21.gif]]
A magic ninja should aim to gather mobs of enemies into as tight a stack as they can before dragging them into the [[Blaze Shield]].
[[File:BSDemo5.gif|center|BSDemo5.gif]]
Allowing them to capitalize on the small 3x3 AoE each target entering the spell produces.
===How to Use the Calculator For Ninja Skills=== Being able to determine what stats/equipment you need to one shot or two shot something is important for leveling or farming as any class. Unfortunately for ninja, none of the stat calculators available are accurate for the majority of our skills given the extent of the changes on Payon Stories. Thankfully there's a fairly easy workaround. Using the PS stat calculator [https://payonrocalc.jaludev.com/ here], ninja can use the ''Basic Attack'' damage figure to calculate the damage of skills like [[Shadow Slash]] and [[Throw Huuma Shuriken]]. [[File:Ninjagptips1.png|thumb|Multiply critical damage by 8, to get [[Shadow Slash]] crit damage]]
[[File:Ninjagptips3.png|thumb|Multiply minimum damage by 3 to get [[Throw Kunai]] minimum damage]]
Note that some monsters in the calculator have different maxHP values than in-game (E.g., Merman). ==Overview==
The '''Novice''' is the starting point for all characters in Ragnarok Online. When you create a new character, you may choose from different Hairstyles and Hair colors. Novices do not incur any EXP penalty upon death, and regain 50% HP when respawning. You may also choose which starting Stats to have. Once Job Level 10, Novices can change into one of the following First Classes:
* [[Swordman]]
* [[Magician]]
* [[Archer]]
* [[Merchant]]
* [[Thief]]
* [[Acolyte]]

Alternatively, they can choose to become an Expanded Class:
* [[Super Novice]]

==Training Grounds==
1. Talk to the '''Shion''', the very first NPC where you spawn. Talk to her '''twice''' to gain +1 base level.

2. Talk to the '''Receptionist''' inside the building, type your character's name then choose ''Apply for training''.

3. Talk to the '''Interfaces Tutor'''. Choose first option until levels are gained.

4. Talk to the '''Item Tutor''', when asked to use [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=569 Novice Potion], '''use it''' for +1 Base Level. When asked to equip [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=2414 Novice Slippers], '''equip it''' for +1 base level.

5. Talk to the '''Kafra Employee'''. Choose ''About Kafra services'' then read the first two options for levels.

6. Talk to the '''Skill Tutor'''. He will give you some experience and teach you the First Aid Skill.

7. Go to the left room and talk to '''Helper''', the left NPC in the combat field room.

8. Talk to the '''Entrance Guard''', the right NPC in the combat field room to warp you to the training field.

9. Here in the Training Field, it is your choice on what monster to kill to gain experience. For access to higher difficulty monsters in the training field, talk to the '''Trainer''' and choose "''I do want more of a challenge~''" or "''I wanna fight tough monsters!''"

*'''Note''': You have the option to die to a random monster or use a [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=12324 Novice Butterfly Wing] in order to go back to the combat field room and gain +1 base level by talking to the '''Entrance Guard''' again.

10. Kill monsters until Job Level 10 or until satisfied then head to the '''Test Examiner''' NPC on the rightmost part of the map to go to the next room.

*'''Note''': Talk to the '''Stat Specialist''' NPC to reset your stat points if necessary.

11. Talk to '''Bruce''' for a quick First Job Class Explanation. Go through any option you want once.

12. Talk to '''Hanson''' and choose if you want to take the Novice Personality Test by choosing the option, "''I'll take the course.''" or going straight to town by choosing the option, "''Let me start Ragnarok Online please.''"

*'''Note''': It is advisable to take the Novice Personality Test for starter gear based on the job that you will get from the test.

==  Description ==
Creates a 3x3 cell cloud around the target cell that blocks the damage all ranged physical attacks. This means that it also blocks the bow attacks of players. Monsters (and player attacks/skills) count as being "ranged" if their attack has a range of 4 or more cells.

Pneuma cannot be cast if it is targeted to overlap an already existing Pneuma area, [[Magnetic Earth]], or a [[Safety Wall]]. It can also be used to prevent a Safety Wall from being created on the target area. Note that '''only''' damage is blocked by Pneuma; other effects like [[Stun]] and [[:Category:Knock_Back_Skills|knockback]] will retain their abilities. It is therefore possible to use [[Arrow Repel]] to knock a player out of a Pneuma and into harm's way.

After 10 seconds, Pneuma will expire. It will be difficult for you to recast pneuma on the same cell quickly, so it is simpler to place 2 pneumas side-by-side and shift when the time is up. The only delay is in the animation, so you can spawn many pneumas to protect many people at once. In a party, remember to pneuma yourself before doing so.

Pneuma completely blocks the following skills:

==Overview==

[[Image: Priest.jpg|thumb|left]]

[[Acolyte]]s who have sworn to give their life to the Gods, adhere to Their teachings and who dedicate themselves to easing the suffering of others can be risen up as priests. As instruments of their miraculous works, priests do well by doing good. Whether they act through others by supporting them, or focus their efforts on destroying evil with their own hands, all priests share a holy calling.

Put simply, no class is as essential as a priest is. In pairs, a priest is capable of more than doubling their partner's offensive power with spells like [[Lex Aeterna]], [[Suffragium]] and [[Aspersio]]. In larger groups, a priest helps both sustain and safeguard the party by boosting SP reserves with [[Magnificat]] and keeping everyone alive through [[Safety Wall]], [[Renew]], and [[Sanctuary]]. Even just the sight of a priest in the streets of Payon or out in the wilderness can be uplifting, as most are more than happy to throw out buffs and heals to those who ask.

Aside from their supportive capabilities, priests are armed with powerful tools to crush [[Demon]]s and the [[Undead]]. A ME priest can decimate entire hordes of evil with [[Magnus Exorcismus]], a TU priest can instantly destroy any [[Undead]] in a single cast of [[Turn Undead]], and battle priests wield the [[Holy Strike]] skill to punish any creature that fears the [[Holy]] element.

==Job change Guide==
''See [[Priest Job Change Guide]] for information.''








==Builds==
=== Magnus Exorcismus Priest===
* STR: 1
* AGI: 1
* VIT: 20+
* INT: 90+
* DEX: 80+
* LUK: 1

Those who want to use powerful [[Holy]] magic to eradicate hordes of evil monsters call themselves Magnus Exorcismus priests. Magnus Exorcismus or "ME priests" are built around the very powerful [[Magnus Exorcismus]] spell. ME priest is generally a solo/mobbing oriented build, and involves gathering groups of [[Demon]] race/[[Undead]] element monsters and repeatedly dragging them through ME until they die. Owing to [[Magnus Exorcismus]]'s very long cast time and the fact that its play style involves tanking their enemies during casts, ME priests only really hit their stride in later levels (85+). Once they reach those levels however, they reap the rewards of a very fast leveling and lucrative character.

ME priests stack INT and DEX to facilitate the 15 second cast time, mATK-based spell. Priests generally aim for 115 or 120 INT total, depending on what they intend to hunt (E.g., 120 INT for Abysmal Knight or Corruptors). Going beyond 120 INT is generally not recommended as the tradeoff to DEX/VIT is too great. The exact amount of VIT vs DEX a ME priest takes is a matter of preference and some debate. DEX increases kill speed and survivability by virtue of reducing the amount of time being hit by enemies while casting ME, whereas VIT helps the priest survive mobs by increasing maximum HP and the shield/heal provided by [[Kyrie Eleison]] and [[Renew]]. Whether a ME priest wants to hunt on maps where [[Stun]] is a potential issue (E.g., Kraben in Ayothaya 02) is an additional consideration for how much VIT is taken.

{| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"
|+ class="nowrap" | Skill Overview
|

Example skill build: [https://tools.payonstories.com/skill?job=Priest&s=Nzk9MTAmMTI9MSY2OD00JjMxPTEmNjY9MyY3MD0zJjI4PTEwJjc4PTEmNzY9NSYyND0xJjc3PTMmNTQ9MSY3Mj0xJjk9NCYzND0xMCYyMj01JjI5PTEwJjMzPTImMjc9MiYyNj0yJg== Here] 19 skill points are left unspent depending on what the ME priest intends to do with their character.

''The following covers skills that may not be straight forward picks, and provides context to help an aspiring ME priest make decisions regarding their build.''

*[[Kyrie Eleison]]: Generally considered the first defense for a ME priest when being beaten on while casting ME. Gains greater value the higher their HP pool.
*[[Renew]]: Can give added survivability to a ME priest when mobbing, and gains greater value the higher their HP pool. Usually the choice is between Renew3/KE10 or KE9/Renew4 given skill point availability after ME and its pre-requisites.
*[[Safety Wall]]: Can be taken in place of Kyrie Eleison to protect a ME priest while casting, though many ME priests generally prefer KE as it is more mobile and economical. Safety Wall can be given additional consideration if the ME priest intends on stacking very low VIT (and thus have lower maxHP) or specifically wants to hunt high HP monsters like Abysmal Knight or Corruptors, as SW is better for those enemies. Safety Wall also blocks certain irritating skills like Armour Destruction, and gains more value the less geared the ME priest is.
*[[Magnificat]]: Given the amount of INT and maxSP that ME priests have, this skill is not usually needed for soloing. A ME priest could consider taking this skill if they want to duo/party frequently. A single point in this skill is a decent compromise for duo/party aspiring ME priests, though constantly recasting it could get annoying.
*[[Turn Undead]]: Should only be taken past rank 3 if the ME priest wants to hybrid as a TU priest (See that section). This skill gains added merit as it makes early leveling easier and a ME/TU priest wouldn't have to rely on groups for those difficult early/mid levels.
*[[Sanctuary]]: Another option alongside [[Safety Wall]] and [[Kyrie Eleison]] for helping to keep you alive while casting ME. Using this skill properly requires carefully placing it so that its charges aren't consumed by damaging the enemy (i.e., so that it is under you, but not in the path of enemies as they approach you casting ME).
*[[Pneuma]]: Is generally skipped as the only place where it is really relevant to a ME priest is in Glast Heim with Raydric Archers. Another small consideration is that it could make early leveling easier by opening Firelock Soldiers as an option. If you intend on using Safety Wall, definitely skip this as the two effects cannot overlap.
*[[Divine Protection]]: Rank 5 is mandatory to learn [[Blessing]], but some consideration should be given to going all the way to rank 10. The "VIT DEF" provided by Divine Protection is not reduced by mob size like regular VIT def is, and scales with Baselvl. The tradeoff for getting more Divine Protection ranks usually means forgoing Pneuma and at least 1 rank of [[Warp Portal]].
|}

===Turn Undead Priest===
* STR: 1
* AGI: 1-60+
* VIT: 25-50+
* INT: 70+
* DEX: 50+
* LUK: 30-99

Priests who have dedicated themselves entirely to eradicating the [[Undead]] take up the mantle of the Turn Undead or "TU" priest. [[Turn Undead]] is a spell that has a high chance to instantly kill any non-boss protocol [[Undead]] enemy in a single hit. TU priests are built entirely around maximizing this skill's success rate (based on INT, Blvl and LUK), and facilitating its use around very specific high health pool [[Undead]] like Anubis, Ancient Mummy or Wraith Dead. 

TU priests can either be [[Flee]]-based or more DEX focused. Even the highest level [[Undead]] have modest [[Flee]] requirements for Priests once debuffed ([[Priest#Debuffing Demons and the Undead]]), so a TU priest can stack AGI aiming for a target [[Flee]] amount ([[Priest#Strategies for TU Priests]]) by a given level. Alternatively, a TU priest can focus on maximizing their cast speed and other stats to make kiting targets while casting [[Turn Undead]] and [[Kyrie Eleison]] more efficient. 

Given the relatively low skill point demands of a TU priest, some may opt to hybrid as Full Support or Magnus Exorcismus priests adjusting their stat/skill build as appropriate.

*[[Renew]]: Generally a better self-sustain option over [[Heal]] for [[Flee]]-based TU priests, as you'll spend less time/actions recovering the same amount of health.
*[[Kyrie Eleison]]: Can help a TU priest survive high damage skills like [[Sonic Blow]].
*[[Gloria]]: This skill is generally only skipped if the TU priest intends to be a ME hybrid.
*[[Warp Portal]]: If you want this skill consider stopping at 2 points, as most TU priests will only frequent a single map in their middle-late levels.
*[[Decrease AGI]]: Can be very useful for VIT/DEX focused TU priest specifically for kiting fast moving undead like Anubis. Success rate increases based on rank used.

*[[Suffragium]]: A must if you intend on supporting casters like [[Wizard]]s especially. Can be skipped otherwise.
*[[Lex Aeterna]]: Useful for supporting any character, but keep in mind it requires ''3'' additional skill points rather than 1 due to its pre-requisites. 
*[[Safety Wall]]: Useful if you intend on supporting party members while MvPing only.

=== Battle Priest===
* STR: 80+
* AGI: 70-99
* VIT: 1
* INT: 1+
* DEX: 30-50
* LUK: 30+

For priests who want to destroy evil by hitting it repeatedly with a stick, Battle Priests (BP) represent the sole physical melee build of the class. Battle priests empower themselves with a huge array of self-buffs and the unique [[Holy Strike]] passive ability. Battle Priests have excellent self-sustain thanks to various priest skills and passives, and make for a great duo partner (especially with [[Blacksmith]]). Owing to [[Holy Strike]] functioning on [[Shadow]] and [[Undead]] element enemies only, BP generally only hunt those types of monsters and will find themselves frequenting Glast Heim, Niflheim, Payon Caves and anywhere else evil makes its lair.

[[Holy Strike]]'s damage scaling increases with base STR and character level, so BP tend to go heavy on STR. AGI helps with DPS and [[Flee]], though BP have an easier time dodging their targets than one would think thanks to their debuffs (see [[Priest#Debuffing Demons and the Undead]]). [[Holy Strike]]'s activation rate is increased by LUK, and so BP usually take a healthy amount of that attribute. A battle priest may opt for lower DEX if they intend on using the [[Acolyte]] or Ancient Mummy card sets.

{| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"

* [[Heal]]: You may opt to get no more than 3 points of this skill as [[Renew]] covers self-sustain quite well, and if you don't intend on using the [[Acolyte]] card set, or Enchanted Peach Tree card.
* [[Cure]]: Can be skipped if more points are needed, as its effect can be replicated with Green Potions or Panacea.
* [[Teleport]]: Can be skipped if more points are needed, as BP have a very high carry weight capacity and can hold many fly wings, and sustaining [[Teleport]] use may require more investment in [[Increase SP Recovery]].

=== Full Support Priest ===
* STR: 1
* AGI: 1
* VIT: 75+
* INT: 60+
* DEX: 70+
* LUK: 1

Full support priests are those for whom doing good means working through others. The quintessential support character, full support (or "FS") priests are an almost mandatory component of any party. Though they don't deal damage themselves, they more than make up for it by boosting the damage and survivability of everyone else in the group. Being a pure support character, FS priests are not capable of hunting or leveling very well on their own.

FS priests don't usually get more than moderate INT, as [[Increase SP Recovery]] 4 and [[Magnificat]] paired with priest's large SP pool is more than enough to sustain their casting in most scenarios. VIT is often the most heavily invested in attribute, as higher amounts aid both the FS priest's durability and resistance to two key status effects ([[Stun]] and [[Silence]]). DEX reduces cast time of buffs like [[Magnificat]], which improves the priest's mobility (handy in a walking party/duo) and ability to quickly fire off [[Safety Wall]]s. Some FS priests may prioritize DEX over VIT.

*[[Signum Crucis]]: May be worth it if an FS priest is certain they're going to be duoing/partying on specific maps with high [[DEF]] [[Demon]] race or [[Undead]] element enemies like Nilfheim field 02 or Odin 01. It should be noted that this skill ''does'' affect boss protocol/MvP monsters, and that many MvPs are [[Demon]] race.
*[[Angelus]]: A solid pick for toughening up tanks (be it a dedicated one, or the FS priest themselves).

=== Magnus Exorcismus Priest ===
Like most casters, ME priests seek out equipment that boosts their INT/mATK and DEX. A Phen Card in any accessory is necessary for [[Magnus Exorcismus]] use, switching to that accessory to prevent your cast from being interrupted and then switching back (via hotkeys, usually). Gyokuto carded headgear will always provide greater cast time reduction to ME than an Apple of Archer will (except at unachievable levels of DEX i.e., 140+), and should generally be a first priority piece of equipment. High defense equipment is beneficial even when mobbing, but is less important than %-reduction gear like Teddy Bear/Khalitzburg carded shields, Raydric carded garments and [[Shadow]]/[[Undead]] damage reducing armor cards like Bathory/Argiope when facing foes who use dangerous skills of that element. The Acolyte Set ([[Active Card Set & Item Combos]]) is a good option for ME priests, especially on maps like Nif Field 01 which have a mix of [[Undead]] and [[Demon]] enemies as the set provides % reduction for both. 

Playing a ME priest without key damage mitigating equipment like Raydric garment or race-reduction shield is challenging, as your ability to level and farm is directly affected by how many enemies you can tank while casting ME. The best recommendation for a new player wanting to be a ME priest is to take [[Safety Wall]] instead of [[Kyrie Eleison]] as part of their skill build, rather than any specific gear suggestions. The protection offered by [[Safety Wall]] becomes more valuable the more damage each individual hit does, at least compared to [[Kyrie Eleison]] and will help offset the lack of expensive protective equipment. 

Aside from the above, a new player should aim for Evil Bone Wand, Crown [0] and either Glove [0] or Earring [0]s are their first investments. A Holy Robe [0] is a relatively affordable high defense armor that provides additional protection against [[Demon]]s. The Necrofantasy set represents a cheaper alternative to Raydric card for damage reduction for [[Undead]] or [[Ghost]] element enemies.

=== Turn Undead Priest ===
Both types of TU priest wear equipment that boosts their INT and LUK (See [[Turn Undead]]). AGI TU priests seek out flee boosting cards/armor (at least for early-mid levels), and DEX TU priests aim to gear for boosting that attribute. TU priests wear shields carded with either Teddy Bear ([[Undead]]) or Thara Frog ([[Demi Human]]), and generally use Arc Wand [2] with either Drops Card (DEX TU) or Lunatic Card (AGI TU) respectively. The Acolyte Set ([[Active Card Set & Item Combos]]) is a decent option for TU priests, especially if acquiring a Teddy Bear card is difficult/expensive.

For newer players making a TU priest, an Evil Bone Wand and Crown [0] are cheap, potent and easy to resell first pickups. For one who plans on killing Anubis, two solid first major investments are a Thara Frog carded Buckler [1] and Poo Poo Hat. AGI TU priests should always consider the dirt cheap Pantie + Undershirt combo. The Necrofantasy set represents a cheaper alternative to Raydric card for damage reduction, as a TU priest's targets are ''always'' [[Undead]] element.

=== Battle Priest ===
Battle Priests generally value the same attributes that most melee do (STR, AGI, DEX, +ATK) but won't need to focus as much on flee as an AGI [[Crusader]] or [[Knight]] might thanks to [[Blessing]]'s debuff potential. Santa Poring, Strouf and Hydra cards are those most typically found carded in BP weapons, but there are alternatives. Owing to the lack of weapon cards that boost damage against [[Undead]], Skeleton Worker carded Chains are a good investment for BP (which are useful to spirit [[Monk]]s too) for killing the majority of [[Undead]] race enemies. The Ancient Mummy set is a good choice generally, or in any scenario where you don't have a race-reduction shield and/or need the +hit that Mummy Card provides. The Acolyte Set ([[Active Card Set & Item Combos]]) is an unbeatable option for BP as far as sustain/survivability is concerned, as it gives 30% damage reduction as well as autocast [[Heal]] 10. if you plan on using this set, make sure you've taken [[Heal]] 10 in your skill build.

For new players or those wanting more universal/budget arms, a Chain [3] with 3 Santa Poring Cards is a good first weapon to make that will deal with many targets that BPs kill. The Ancient Mummy combo might also be worth considering as a solid cost-effective option, given the relative affordability of both cards. Aside from those two, the Acolyte Set is a reasonable investment BP, especially if you have other priests as they can share that equipment/set (other than the weapon).

===  Full Support Priest ===
FS priests generally prioritize ''not dying'' when it comes to their equipment. A dead FS priest can't save or buff anyone else, and so for most FS priests DEF, MDEF, %damage reduction and anything that boosts their VIT/maxHP tends to be how they gear. Aside from focusing on their survivability, FS priests will stack +DEX as that is usually their highest base attribute. For MvPing, special consideration should be made for boss skills that destroy armor (Cornutus Card) or deal heavy elemental damage (E.g., Bathory Card, Pasana Card). FS priests are the least inclined to use the Acolyte Set, as their choice of shield varies depending on with who they duo/party with. Generally a good idea in parties for many characters, a Smokie carded accessory is an especially good choice for FS priests whether in a duo (if they aren't tanking) or a party.

If new or on a budget, npc purchased gear upgraded to +4 can serve as a reasonable starting point for boosting survivability, as priests have access to surprisingly high defense equipment like Biretta and Saint's Robe. Good first investments include a Pupa Card and Thief Bug Egg cards as they are cheap and provide a large static boost to maxHP.

===Turn Undead Priest===
''' Recommended Skill Progression '''
*[[Increase SP Recovery]] 4
*[[Status Recovery]] 1
*[[Resurrection]] 1
*[[Lex Divina]] 3
*[[Turn Undead]] 10
*[[Magnificat]] 3
*[[Kyrie Eleison]] 4
*[[Gloria]] 5

''' Recommended Stat Progression '''
*AGI TU: You should stack INT until you reach the base value in your planned final build (or near it), get ~20 DEX, then AGI until you reach a given threshold for a target (See: [[Priest#Strategies for TU Priests]]). ~20 DEX is a bit painful, but sufficient until your INT and AGI are at where they need to be. From that point on, it depends on your final build. LUK, regardless of how much you plan on getting, is generally the last thing you max.

*DEX TU: You should stack INT until ~65-70 base, then DEX to ~50 and VIT to ~20. From that point on, it depends on your final build. LUK, regardless of how much you plan on getting, is generally the last thing you max.

=== Full Support Priest ===
''' Recommended Skill Progression '''
*''As FS priest builds vary greatly, skill progression will depends on the selections made by the priest (See the skill overview at [[Priest#Full Support Priest]]). Generally [[Magnificat]], [[Status Recovery]], [[Aspersio]], [[Gloria]] and [[Lex Aeterna]] are the most widely used and impactful support skills and are typically gotten first.''

''' Recommended Stat Progression '''
* INT to the 60s/70s (base value) is usually fine for sustaining SP (particularly with [[Magnificat]] active) and is a good idea to get first. 40-50 VIT and 30+ DEX afterwards will allow you to survive reasonably well and not lag behind while in tow with a party/duo in most places. From that point on it depends on your final build, but generally VIT to your final value is more of a priority than DEX (which can be peppered in but finished last).  

{| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"
|+ class="nowrap" | FS Duo Suggestions
|
<center>''The following is by no means a comprehensive list of duo possibilities, but some of the more popular choices for FS priests.''</center>

''ABB Hunter''
*ABB excel at killing things with high flee/DEF, and duos with them are best in places with monsters that fit that description. Some examples being GH Chiv 01, Turtle Dungeon, TI Surface, Goats/Harpies, Sleepers/Demon Pungus, etc. Aside from agi+bless, [[Gloria]] benefits these hunters enormously because of how auto [[Blitz Beat]] works.

''Crit Sin''
* Critical [[Assassin]]s tend to favour high flee/DEF enemies like ABB hunters do, but benefit more from a duo with an FS priest in maps where they can take advantage of [[Aspersio]]. Maps like Odin 01, GH Chiv and Niff Field 01/02 are common spots for these duos. [[Gloria]] can be helpful for crit sins if they don't reach 100% crit on their own, or rely on Bonechewer Card to do so. An FS priest can help crit sins AoE mobs they otherwise wouldn't be able to because they can see through [[Hiding]] status by tanking those groups for them.

''AGI Knight/Sader''
* Much like crit sins, these characters tend to favour duos with FS priests in areas where the [[Holy]] element is helpful (see the above). A knight with an overupgraded Dragon Slayer or Gae Bolg can do especially well with an FS priest in tow somewhere like Abyss. 

''Wizard''
* A good option for FS priests who opted to take [[Suffragium]]. Generally the priest gathers mobs, uses [[Suffragium]] on the wizard who then fires off a hasted [[Storm Gust]]. Popular maps for this duo are CT High Orcs, Orc Village High Orcs, Majoruros and Magma 01.

''GC Crusader''
* An FS priest pairs very with a GC sader as both [[Blessing]] and [[Magnificat]] go a long way towards solving their endless SP management woes. A buffed up GC sader who doesn't have to worry about damage taken or their SP pool is a supercharged killer in GH Chiv, Tamruan, Niff Field 01 and any other map they typically frequent.

==Gameplay Tips==
===Debuffing Demons and the Undead===
Certain [[Acolyte]] and Priest beneficial spells have negative effects when used against [[Demon]] race or [[Undead]] '''element''' enemies. Making use of these spells as debuffs can give the user an extra edge against these foes.

'''Acolyte'''
*[[Blessing]]: Reduces [[Demon]] race and [[Undead]] element DEX and INT by 50% for the skill duration (100% success rate).
*[[Heal]]: Deals half its normal healing amount as [[Holy]] damage to [[Undead]] element only. The damage it deals is modified by the target's [[Undead]] element level (e.g., 200% weakness to [[Holy]] for [[Undead]] 4 monsters). Using [[Heal]] to damage [[Undead]] is commonly referred to as "Heal bombing".

'''Priest'''
*[[Status Recovery]]: Blinds [[Undead]] element only by chance (see skill page for formula). Blinded [[Undead]] will de-aggro any target it was attacking/chasing, providing they don't get too close.
*[[Aspersio]]: Deals minor [[Holy]] damage when cast on [[Demon]] race and [[Undead]] element.
*[[Resurrection]]: When used on [[Undead]] element only this skill becomes the same rank of [[Turn Undead]] (e.g., Using rank 2 [[Resurrection]] casts rank 2 [[Turn Undead]]).

===Strategies for TU Priests===
'''AGI TU'''

Flee-based TU priests always start on an [[Undead]] by [[Blessing]] them first to reduce their hit rate. If flee still isn't high enough to 95% dodge the [[Undead]], they can also be blinded with [[Status Recovery]]. AGI TU priests should plan their build's base AGI value around what +flee equipment they have access to, such as with the following example with 76 AGI and Anubis:

76 AGI at level 70 = 95% flee with Whisper Card + Steel Chonchon Pet + [[Blessing]] debuff
<br>76 AGI at level 80 = 95% flee with Necrofantasy Set + Steel Chonchon Pet + [[Blessing]] debuff
<br>76 AGI at level 90 = 95% flee with Steel Chonchon Pet + [[Blessing]] debuff
<br>76 AGI at level 95 = 95% flee with [[Blessing]] debuff

With the priest being able to trade out flee equipment for success rate (i.e., +INT/LUK) boosting gear or damage reduction gear (e.g., Raydric) as they reach higher levels.

'''DEX TU'''

The general strategy for DEX-based TU priests is to kite [[Undead]] while casting [[Turn Undead]]. Fast cast speed is leveraged to keep [[Kyrie Eleison]] up (even while kiting mobs at mid-late levels) to make this easier/faster. DEX TU generally don't bother [[Blessing]] their targets first like AGI TU do, unless they have harmful damaging spells as [[Blessing]] will halve their INT.

'''Multiple Undead'''

The most popular TU targets (Anubis, Ancient Mummy, Wraith Dead) move too fast for you to be able to cast [[Turn Undead]] on them and get away without being attacked at least once, regardless of DEX. This becomes a problem when there are several of your target in one place as spawns of these [[Undead]] on any given map are scarce (only 15/20 at most). Being able to manage groups of them is important for leveling as a TU priest.

The best strategy for dealing with multiple [[Undead]] is to [[Status Recovery]] them after [[Blessing]] them, as the success rate of blinding them is improved by halving their INT stat with bless. Even normally aggressive [[Undead]] are pacified once blinded, allowing you to deal with each enemy one at a time.

1. Apply to become a '''Priest''' in the [[Prontera]] Church ''(prt_church 16, 41)'' by speaking to '''Bishop Paul'''.

2. You must visit all three Ascetics from the [[Acolyte Job Change Guide|Acolyte Job Quest]]. However, this step may be skipped by '''Job Level 50 Acolytes'''.

3. After returning from the three Ascetics, Bishop Paul grants you access to a room where the next two tests will take place: Exorcism and Temptation.

4. In this room, click '''Peter S. Alberto''' multiple times to activate his dialogue window. The excessive clicking required is actually part of the test, not a bug. A '''[[Priest]]''' can come along to help for these two tests by following the same instructions and bringing a [[Image:2608.png]] [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=2608 Rosary] in their inventory ''(not equipped)''.

5. In the next few rooms, defeat all the [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=monster&action=view&id=1015 Zombie] that appear. All must be killed in each room to clear the Exorcism stage and move onto Temptation.

6. Successfully walk past four NPCs (''Deviruchi'', ''Doppleganger'', ''Dark Lord'', and finally ''Baphomet'') without accepting their deals. Some may offer bribes or insist Priest life is too difficult to be worthwhile, but choose options that reject their offers.

7. Following this is another series of rooms where [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=monster&action=view&id=1015 Zombies] spawn, with [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=monster&action=view&id=1041 Mummies] mixed in. It is not necessary to kill them all, simply run by.

8. After exiting the last room, you'll be warped back to Bishop Paul. He suggests speaking with '''Sister Cecelia''' on the other side of the room. Employ common sense to answer her questions with holy and righteous responses to pass it.

9. Return to Bishop Paul to become a '''[[Priest]]''' after a bit of dialogue. He will reward Job Level 50 Acolytes with a [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=1551 Bible[2<nowiki>]</nowiki>], while those below Job 50 will receive a [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=1550 Book[3<nowiki>]</nowiki>].

== Description ==
Provoke lowers an opponent's [[DEF|defense]] and increases their [[ATK|attack]] for 30 seconds.

!Level || Enemy +[[ATK]] || -Enemy [[DEF]] || Success Chance || SP Cost

== Notes ==
*The success rate of Provoke increases when used on monsters when the user's level is greater than that of the monster. The greater the level gap between the two, the greater the increase to success rate as per the formula: 50+3*Skill_level+LevelDifferential
*Against players, only their [[VIT]] defense is lowered. 
*[[Undead]] and [[Boss]]-type monsters cannot be [[Provoke|provoked]].
*Using Provoke on any monster or (enemy) player that is [[Frozen]] will break them out of that status.
*Aloevera allows a user to cast level 1 Provoke when consumed.

== Strategies ==
=== PvM ===
*Provoke can be used to aggravate monsters without dealing damage to them. This is helpful for tanking low level monsters for other players. 
*Provoking monsters with a high level of Provoke will weaken them considerably, allowing much more damage to be dealt to them (unless the player is levelling with defense-ignoring or formula-flipping skills or weapons, such as an Ice Pick).
*Provoke counts as a "hit" (or rude attack) on a monster that is fiberlocked, behind an icewall, or otherwise can't reach the player, (if it is not a boss or undead monster) and will cause it to teleport.

=== PvP ===
*Although Provoke can weaken monsters considerably, it is often unwise to use it on opponents in [[PvP]]. They will gain an [[ATK]] boost for a minor [[VIT]]-defense loss. Allies can benefit from it in many ways though. 
*Provoking players that do not benefit from an [[ATK]] boost with the intent of doing more damage to them may also not be wise if you or party members would normally deal more damage with an Ice Pick or skill/weapon of that type. 
*However, Provoke is a good method for interrupting casts, especially during [[WoE]] where Phen accessories are disabled. Provoke also works in stopping a [[Sacrifice|Sacrificed]] opponent's cast, which would otherwise be uninterruptible. Level 1 Provoke can be used here to conserve SP unless there is a large level difference.
*Note that Provoke fails against Evil Druid armored players. This can hint for the use of a holy or fire endow/weapon for boosted damage.

== Description ==
Sacrifice yourself in order to revive all [[party]] members near you. The skill will affect any [[party]] member within a 15 * 15 area around you, and they will all be revived with 50% [[HP]]. When successful, this skill reduces your [[HP]] and [[SP]] to 1, and you lose 1% of your Base [[EXP]]. For each person you revive with the skill however, the penalty is reduced by 0.2% exp. With 5 or more people, you do not suffer any [[EXP]] penalty. If you do not have enough [[EXP]] to cast this skill, it will fail.

== For Level 99 Characters ==
Characters at level 99 still receive experience which can be seen on the character select screen. This [[EXP]] never decreases due to death, so it should continue to rise as the character obtains [[EXP]] as usual. This [[EXP]] is used when casting Redemptio; resurrecting less than five people will reduce the [[EXP]] shown in the character select screen. The [[EXP]] required to resurrect is 1% of the 99,999,999 maximum, or equal to 1 million, as a whole; each person resurrected reduces the cost by 200,000 EXP.

==Overview==

[[Image: Rogue.jpg|thumb|left]]

Sly and ruthless, rogues weaponize their cunning to take the underhanded techniques of [[Thief|thieves]] and elevate them to new heights.  

The rogue is a master of taking what isn’t theirs. They can rob their foes of their loot with [[Snatcher]], divest them of their equipment with skills like [[Strip Weapon]], and even steal their abilities with the incredibly versatile [[Plagiarism]]. By no means limited to thievery, a rogue will wield dagger, sword or bow to strike at their foes with deadly precision, exploiting their foes weaknesses using the [[Back Stab]] and [[Trick Arrow]] skills.

Though often seen on their own, Rogues can also fill a valuable support role in PvP, WoE, and MvP through their strip skills. In guild dungeon parties, their high Flee and [[Quick Step]] skill makes them excellent mobbers. Dedicated [[Back Stab]] rogues are capable of very high DPS in parties, and certain builds can even supplement other's group roles by copying abilities.

== Builds ==


===Gank/Snatcher Rogue===

* STR: 70+
* AGI: 99
* VIT: 1
* INT: 1
* DEX: 50-65 
* LUK: 1

A popular choice of farming character for both new players and veterans alike. The gameplay usually revolves around auto-attacking to trigger plagiarised abilities, autocast cards like [[Corruptor Card]] and [[Snatcher]] to steal extra loot. These rogues have excellent self-sustain and map variety, making for an ideal character in solo play.

Most Gank rogues opt for more AGI over STR, so as to maximize the opportunities for [[Snatcher]] to trigger. Gank Rogues can also aim for 110 or 120 total STR with the intent of maximizing the effectiveness of skills like [[Acid Terror]], [[Demonstration]], or [[Bowling Bash]]. Aside from its usual benefits, DEX investment for a gank rogue is typically higher than most autoattackers would get because the success rate of [[Snatcher]] is increased as a function of dexterity.

Suggested [[Plagiarism]] skills: [[Heal]], [[Aspersio]], [[Bowling Bash]], [[Triple Attack]], [[Holy Cross]], [[Acid Terror]], [[Demonstration]]

The [https://tools.payonstories.com/skill?state=eJxllE1r3jAMx79Lzj10jMF4boqtJFr8ksl2nqZjGAZlMAo9jO1S%2Bt2nFDtO16N%2Bkay3v%2FLc%2FXr60V06fvr556G76R4f%2Fj48%2Fu4u3547MHnyZjM0TrG7fHi5OVCITDNWZrPG6B1EzwVZlY1PujkwBp9YnUJ68hgnUqGFqAnciAo4nphYGpVniPiWMq7epEjeNX6PblvIqQm5ZRKjJ0X6SG5M7tNGbsxBSq54YalSo13kyer5WhOPCMz%2B2qCFWaL%2Fg0FBjMjyobA45LCIPRsM4HSjcZJASe2OikJe0Xk7Oxqw%2BfWg5mBIv3lyIYFvY4N3pEApNIX1kBcZ5erpmHgf8siIupnJDUBsNlmlmgsONkOKvkcOyCdo%2FSpFsOxhRd4KV5zDtPfX%2FAaIYHpzjEWrfBWHfYi2oCnmRfYcIVhShbkv8hJofxVv0URd6Ozq%2BGPNYceMDnnclIdDJT7PFBlcMHCWg5cBmnnz6Rgfj1kZH6QNN9AxQaFf0%2BtUcWmoNzJ9CzxjzRMgo0GLLl5FjPye0rHkBkeW%2FO%2FxQIfuBCqWFveqGhrF7U6aUjX79T6H%2FRClrtCyu1W2n8zAcJKIpbBf1W0xtU%2B9wROQeDAneyoS%2B1wl5instVR7v%2B47GureRetrMjHtHdyWacXkHBrNtAr8WCADSeefikUukiX9eseVLQZGAqZgazlB5CE%2FC%2BT1tJ5RxHxqWkiQv0258tuX7y%2F%2FALCEXq0%3D following] represents the basic skeleton of a typical gank rogue, with 14 points left unspent. Solid choices include any of the strip skills, [[Sword Mastery]], [[Back Stab]] or even [[Compulsion Discount]] (if you are certain you never want to make a character expressly for this purpose).

=== Back Stab Rogue ===

* STR: 90+
* AGI: 70+
* VIT: 1
* INT: 30-60
* DEX: 20-40
* LUK: 1

As sly as any other rogue, but with muscle to back up their cunning. These rogues are excellent in groups as supporting DPS, wielding [[Back Stab]] to its full potential with both a focus on boosting its damage and the SP regen to sustain its use. When solo, these rogues rely primarily on skill use, aiming to effiently one-hit kill targets or AoE mobs of foes down.

In contrast to gank rogues, these characters prioritise STR aiming to hit 120 (usually) total strength with gear and JobLvl bonuses. This greater focus on STR allows them to more easily one hit targets with skills, or else minimize the number of hits needed to kill enemies. AGI is still important, both because most skill delay is ASPD-based, and because alongside [[Improve Dodge]] they can easily FLEE most monsters. Some amount of INT is taken, depending on what kind of SP-related gear (E.g., Ninja Suit combo, Magmawhip, Moonlight Sword) the rogue has access to (See also: [[Rogue#SP Regen Breakpoints]]). DEX is of lesser importance compared to other other builds, because they are neither casting spells nor constantly trying to [[Steal]]. Also, [[Back Stab]] cannot miss. 

Suggested [[Plagiarism]] skills: [[Heal]], [[Aspersio]], [[Bowling Bash]], [[Holy Cross]], [[Acid Terror]], [[Demonstration]]

The [https://tools.payonstories.com/skill?state=eJxllE2L3DAMhv9LznvY0hbK3BRbSdT4I5XtzGZLMRSGQlnYQ2kvy%2F73KtM4znSPeiJZX6%2Fy0vx8%2Ft6cGn7%2B8fvS3DVPlz%2BXp1%2FN6etLAyYP3iyG%2BiE2p3evdzsKkWnEwmzWGL2D6HlDVmXjk64OjMEnVoeQljzGgVSoIWoA16MCjgcmlkblGSLeUsbZmxTJu8of0S following] represents the basic skeleton of a typical back stab rogue build, with 10 points left unspent. [[Sword Mastery]] is most commonly where those remaining points go, but there is merit to grabbing the strip skills at the cost of some points in that passive.

=== Bow Rogue (AGI) ===

* STR: 1
* AGI: 99
* VIT: 1
* INT: 1+
* DEX: 90+
* LUK: 1

Archers with a twist. AGI Bow Rogues can either leisurely auto-attack at a distance, reaping more loot with [[Snatcher]] or make use of [[Plagiarism]] to do things no other bow-wielder can like dispatch hordes of foes with [[Bowling Bash]] or pierce high DEF targets with [[Acid Terror]]. 

Most AGI Bow Rogues will prioritize DEX over AGI, as being ranged they have less of a reliance on flee and will get greater returns on damage and skill-efficiency via DEX. Some AGI Bow Rogues elect to take a bit of INT (in multiples of 6) to support skill-use (see: [[Rogue#SP_Regen_Breakpoints]]).

Suggested [[Plagiarism]] skills: [[Heal]], [[Bowling Bash]], [[Triple Attack]], [[Acid Terror]], [[Demonstration]], [[Holy Cross]], [[Double Strafing]]

The [https://tools.payonstories.com/skill?state=eJxllE2L3DAMhv9LznvYUgplboqtJGr8kcp2ZrOlGApDoSzsobSXZf57lSGOM92jnkjW16u8Nb9efzSnhl9%2F%2Frk0D83L5e%2Fl5Xdz%2BvbWgMmDN4uhfojN6cP1YUchMo1YmM0ao3cQPW%2FIqmx80tWBMfjE6hDSksc4kAo1RA3gelTA8cDE0qg8Q8R7yjh7kyJ5V%2FkzumUi following] represents the basic skeleton of a typical bowgue build, with 5 points left unspent. A bow rogue that doesn't intend on using [[Snatcher]] can ditch all 10 points of that skill.

=== Bow/Caster Rogue (INT) ===

* STR: 1
* AGI: 1-60
* VIT: 1
* INT: 80+
* DEX: 90+
* LUK: 1

Unmatched in versatility, probably the most noteworthy aspect of Caster Rogues is the enormous list of viable [[Plagiarism]] skills they can make use of. Unique among rogues, Bow/Casters are also arguably ''better'' at using certain skills than their original owner. [[Acid Terror]], [[Grand Cross]] as well as any other copyable skill that relies on ATK and has a cast time component these rogues will excel at using, thanks to their reliance on DEX for both ATK as well as cast time reduction.

For casting spells, most will want to build their rogue with as much INT and DEX as possible, but getting ~50 AGI or more to capitalize on the innately high flee that rogues have is also an option. Another alternative is to go a little lower on INT (80 total) if you want to use the WELDER card. Access to Magmawhip Card and higher innate SP also means these Rogues have an easier time sustaining their SP when trapping, meaning the need for INT is lesser than a trap [[Hunter]].

Example [[Plagiarism]] skills: [[Blast Mine]], [[Claymore Trap]], [[Land Mine]], [[Storm Gust]], [[Lord of Vermilion]], [[Water Ball]], [[Acid Terror]], [[Demonstration]], [[Magnus Exorcismus]], [[Turn Undead]], [[Blaze Shield]], [[Bowling Bash]], [[Grand Cross]], [[Holy Cross]]

The [https://tools.payonstories.com/skill?state=eJxllE2L3DAMhv9LznvYUgplboqtJGr8kcp2ZrNLMRSGQlnYQ2kvy%2Fz3KtM4znaPeiJZX6%2Fy2vx8%2Bd6cGn758fvS3DXPlz%2BX51%2FN6em1AZMHbxZD%2FRCb04fr3Y5CZBqxMJs1Ru8get6QVdn4pKsDY%2FCJ1SGkJY9xIBVqiBrA9aiA44GJpVF5hohvKePsTYrkXeWP6J following] represents the basic skeleton of a typical INT/DEX rogue, with 24 points left unspent. Popular choices for remaining points include the strip skills, [[Vulture's Eye]] (unless you are sure you won't be using [[Double Strafing]] or ever autoattacking), and [[Compulsion Discount]] (if you are certain you never want to make a character expressly for this purpose).

== Equipment ==

===Gank/Snatcher Rogue Gear===

Gank rogues tend to use gear that maximize their ASPD (and thus [[Snatcher]] and autocast activations), ATK damage and flee in that order of priority. Carded Gladius [3] or [[Blacksmith]]-forged elemental Damascus are generally the most commonly used weapon for these types of rogues. For using purely ATK-based damage skills like [[Acid Terror]] and [[Demonstration]], a weapon carded with Andre or Zipper Bear cards is ideal (generally in a Saber [3]).

When plagiarising [[Heal]], a shield carded with an Enchanted Peach Tree card can help sustain the Rogue's HP and SP. Gank Rogues could also consider investing in a moonlight dagger on any map they don't intend on using weapon endows. 

The first investments for gank rogues are usually vvs elemental damascus, a Gladius [3] (3x Goblin cards) that can be used on many valuable mobs (wild rose, minorous, spring rabbit) or the aforementioned enchanted peach tree shield. A Poring Dagger is also a reasonable option that can be used on valuable low level [[Snatcher]] targets like Myst Case.

=== Back Stab Rogue Gear ===
Back Stab rogues prioritize +STR/ATK equipment over other attribute boosting gear. Similar to other skill-spamming builds, back stab rogues make great use of +maxSP/SP regen gear like Sohee or Eggyra card, as well as SP refunding items like Magmawhip Card. Back Stab rogues can also use the Ninja Suit + Shinobi Sash combo for a 20% SP cost reduction on all skills. For [[Acid Terror]] or [[Demonstration]] use, 3x Andre Cards in Saber [3] is generally ideal alongside FUEL-carded Boots. For using [[Raid]] or [[Back Stab]], YSER Card in boots are typically used.

In terms of weapons, for most targets (particularly large/medium) properly carded Saber [3] or Blade [4] are ideal in terms of damage. However, the difference between those weapons and similarly carded Gladius [3] is slight, and it may be more practical to simply use daggers as buying or selling carded 1H swords is often difficult by comparison (and daggers are used by many more builds/classes).

Unlike gank or bow rogues, back stab rogues are entirely skill-use based and generally not recommended for newer players as key equipment either boosting their damage (i.e., properly carded weapons) or easing their SP woes (ninja suit combo, magmawhip, etc) are essential for them to be efficient.

=== Bow Rogue (AGI) Gear ===

AGI Bow Rogues use gear that increases their DEX and ATK primarily, as well as their AGI and flee. Gakkung Bow [2] and Arbalest [2] are typically used by AGI Bow Rogues, with Andre/Zipper Bear, or elemental%/racial% cards depending on whether they're using those bows for auto attacking, [[Acid Terror]]/[Demonstration]], or other skills. Repeating Crossbow [1] can also be used as a cheap option for auto-attacking thanks to it being npc-purchasable and having a 3 cell bonus range.

For auto-attacking and [[Snatcher]], shoes with a Great Snake card can be useful to avoid the range restriction on bows and that skill. FUEL carded-shoes can be used for [[Acid Terror]] use.

Bow/Caster Rogues usually have two sets of equipment: An INT/mATK set for spell-based copied skills and DEX equipment somewhat similar to AGI Bow Rogues for ATK-based copied skills. Andre cards can be put into Gakkung Bow [2] or Arbalest [2] for [[Acid Terror]] and [[Demonstration]], and elemental%/racial% cards can be used for skill-use. == Gameplay Tips ==

=== Map Control With Intimidate ===

[[Intimidate]] teleports the rogue and target hit to another location on the map. This skill can be used on certain maps to displace or "cage" troublesome enemies like Ridewords, Mimics and Dragon Tails. Keep in mind that maps will reset if there is no one present on them for 10 minutes.

Maps where [[Intimidate]] can be used (not an exhaustive list):
* Marionette Map - Marionettes have individual spawns in the 4 islands of the map. That means if you teleport away the Ridewords/Dark Frames in one island, all that will be left are marionettes who respawn immediately, allowing for easy farming.
* Turtle Island Surface - The small island to the northeast has a very narrow, winding land bridge connecting it. Dragon Tail can be herded or teleported to the island and will likely stay there for up to hours at a time because of the narrow bridge. 
* Clock Tower Penomena/Cramp map - The walled off water area in the south part of the map has 7 guaranteed cramp spawns. If you teleport away any penomena in the area, the only enemies you'll have left are drainliars and those guarantee cramp spawns (1 min spawn timer). This makes for easier Cramp card farming.

=== Plagiarism and Evil Druid Armor ===
A rogue can only copy skills if they damage them. Certain [[Priest]]/[[Acolyte]] skills damage [[Undead]] element targets, rogues can take advantage of this by wearing armor slotted with the Evil Druid card to learn those skills.

[[File:Evil_Druid_Card.png|center]]

The following skills can be copied only while wearing Evil Druid armor:

* [[Heal]]
* [[Sanctuary]]
* [[Aspersio]]
* [[Ruwach]]
* [[B.S Sacramenti]]
* [[Magnus Exorcismus]]
* [[Turn Undead]]
* [[Resurrection]]* (not on Payon Stories as this skill's ability to one-hit [[Undead]] by low chance was disabled)

== Description ==
Protects a Party Member by taking all of the damage inflicted on said Party Member. The Party Member must be within 10 levels of the caster. The damage that the caster receives from Sacrifice is affected by the Party Member`s [[DEF|Defense]], rather than the caster's. However, if the caster activates [[Auto Guard]], [[Reflect Shield]], or [[Defender]], these skills will also affect Party Members targeted by Sacrifice and will generally function as if the Sacrificed party members had them as well.

== Notes ==
*If a player goes beyond the range of Sacrifice, their line of Sacrifice will graphically disappear. Sacrifice does not deactivate until a player takes damage when out of range of the skill, or the duration of the skill expires. 
*Cannot be cast on other [[Crusader]]s. 
*When a player is Sacrificed, none of their skills can be interrupted by physical or magical attacks as they are not actually receiving any damage. However, certain skills such as [[Provoke]] bypass this protective effect.
*If the Crusader receives damage that exceeds their remaining HP through Sacrifice, they will die, and any damage exceeding the Crusader's hit points does not pass to the original target receiving the damage. 
*Certain abilities function through Sacrifice: [[Auto Guard]], [[Reflect Shield]], and [[Defender]]. [[Auto Guard]] works as if the sacrificed target had the skill active, also inducing physical attack delay when activated. [[Reflect Shield]] only works on melee skills when applied through Sacrifice. This includes [[Guillotine Fist]], as well as [[Arrow Shower]] cast by a monster. [[Defender]] currently will slow all sacrificed targets when activated, but only apply a reduced damage reduction (30%) compared to the 80% reduction on the caster. 
*Refreshing Sacrifice (recasting it on a sacrificed target before its duration ends) requires that the number of players currently being sacrificed is at least 1 less than your limit.

== Applications ==

Safety Wall can be used to easily tank low [[ASPD]] monsters in PVM environments. High ASPD monsters can also be dealt with if the user is capable of casting Safety Wall fast enough once it is consumed, or by simply casting a new Safety Wall in a neighboring cell and moving when the previous SW is about to expire. It is less effective for tanking multiple monsters, as it will quickly consume the Safety Wall. This is highly effective for tanking [[MVP]]s, as long as its mob can be tanked by a separate character.

In [[PvP]], Safety Wall is useful for tanking offensive melee skills such as [[Guillotine Fist]], [[Martyr's Reckoning]] or [[Enchant Deadly Poison]]'d [[Sonic Blow]]. For this to be effective, the user requires sufficient [[DEX]] to cast Safety Wall quickly before the attack occurs. [[Magnetic Earth]] and [[Ganbantein]] can remove Safety Walls.

== Notes ==
* Any amount of damage incoming from a single melee attack or skill will be completely blocked by Safety Wall, regardless of strength.
* Safety Wall only blocks incoming damage. It doesn't protect against status effects and knockback, unless they were side effects of a blocked attack.
* Against melee monsters, Safety Wall will block all melee attacks, melee skills, and some long-ranged defined skills if they were used in melee range (an exception to this is [[Clashing Spiral]] - even if the monster is beside the player, Safety Wall no longer blocks it as of summer 2008).

==Overview==

[[Image: Sage.jpg|thumb|left]]

''Knowledge is power'', but for sages, the pursuit of knowledge is more than just a means to an end; it's a passion and a lifelong endeavour, a path they seek to follow and hope never to reach its end. Sages are [[Mage]]s who seek higher learning after having graduated from the academy in Juno. They're a hybrid support / damage dealing class, as much a boon to allies as they are a bane to their enemies. 

A master of the elements, sages can enchant the weapons of any party member with [[Fire]], [[Water]], [[Earth]] and [[Wind]], better empowering them to dispatch a chosen foe. Sages are likewise able to manipulate the element of monsters as well, using [[Elemental Change]] to alter their very nature. The three land spells: [[Violent Gale]], [[Deluge]] and [[Volcano]] are potent buffs that make sages a welcome addition to any party.

Sages empower their [[Mage]] spellcasting with their supportive spells, as well as the potent [[Double Bolt]] to make them one of the most effective "One hit killers" in the game. They can also utilize the unique [[Hindsight]] skill, using it to fight as a kind of melee/caster hybrid, raining bolts down on their enemies as they strike at them armed with their special book weapons. Though often desired by them, a sage is no by no means reliant on groups as they are effective soloers, capable of surviving even the deadly Muspelheim all on their own.

==Builds==
=== Bolter ===
* STR: 1
* AGI: 1 or 50+
* VIT: 1+
* INT: 99
* DEX: 80+
* LUK: 1

Strong, mobile and flexibile, the Bolter Sage is a character both very new player friendly and extremely effective in the right hands. Bolt sages leverage their [[Double Bolt]] buff to elevate their [[Mage]] spellcasting to new heights, more than doubling their damage when used alongside their potent land skills. A Bolt sage has a tool for every situation, and is always a welcome addition to parties offering excellent utility alongside their offensive capabilities.

Bolter Sages are built as either "Pure INT/DEX" or "AGI Bolters". INT/DEX Bolters invest almost all their points into INT and DEX, aiming to maximize their cast time and by extension their DPS. AGI bolters on the other hand capitalize on the considerable flee boost provided by [[Free Cast]] and [[Violent Gale]], and stack moderate AGI to allow them to reach 95% dodge on a large variety of targets. 

An AGI bolter is usually built around the WELDER card, and will go no higher than 80 in DEX or AGI, to benefit from the card's bonuses. The WELDER card has 3 effects: It reduces cast time by 10% at DEX <= 80, increases MATK by 10% at INT <= 80, and increases FLEE by 20 at AGI <= 80. All Bolter Sages, regardless of type, will typically get ~99 base INT to reach the higher MATK bonuses.

''Other sage builds focused around a single skill/purpose like [[Abracadabra]] or Endows ([[Flame Launcher]], [[Lightning Loader]], etc) are for all intents and purposes similar to bolters, aside from acquiring those skills.''

<center>''The following covers skills that may not be straight forward picks, and provides context to help aspiring bolt sages make decisions regarding their build. Skill choice generally does not differ between INT/DEX and AGI bolt sages''</center>


*[[Increase SP Recovery]]: Even at 120 INT, a sage's natural SP recovery isn't enough to keep up with constant [[Soul Strike]] spam in a map like UT2, or frequent [[Elemental Change]] usage on enemies like Corruptors or Frus. Furthermore, Increase SP Recovery helps keep [[Energy Coat]]'s damage mitigation at its maximum. There is no real consensus on how many points are "enough" for those three purposes. At the very least it could be considered a dump for remaining points, with up to 10 points still being beneficial if you have that many to spare. If you are building your sage purely for group situations or do not intend on using those skills often, you could skip this entirely.
*[[Fire Bolt]]: Though at first glance a "must pick" for a ''Bolt''er Sage, some sages opt to skip this spell as there are no accessory cards that boost its effect the same way Siroma or Conductring boost [[Cold Bolt]] and [[Lightning Bolt]] respectively. 
*[[Fire Ball]]: A strong [[Fire]] AoE, this skill is more DPS on single targets than [[Fire Bolt]] even with [[Double Bolt]] active (assuming no [[A Poem of Bragi]]). Though a popular pick, you may opt to skip it or only take 5 points for [[Fire Wall]] as its usefulness falls off compared to [[Heaven's Drive]] as your cast speed improves, particularly in many popular party maps like Turtle Dungeon.
*[[Fire Wall]]: Even with Sage's mobility via [[Free Cast]], Fire Wall serves as a useful defensive and mobbing tool, as well as a potent [[Undead]] killer. A vertical Fire Wall (See [[Sage#Vertical_Fire_Wall]]) can keep mobs in place for [[Heaven's Drive]] usage, and deal very high [[Fire]] DPS to any [[Undead]] or Boss protocol enemy. Fire Wall can help control mobs of enemies, or enemies that move faster than even a sped up Sage like the very fast enemies in Muspelheim where this spell excels.
*[[Frost Diver]]: This spell is empowered when buffed with the [[Deluge]] effect, increasing its success rate and adding a lingering movement speed slow even should it fail to [[Freeze]]. If you can spare the points (go either 0 or 10), it can save you in a pinch or combo well with [[Lightning Bolt]] and Conductring accessories. It is especially helpful in a difficult map like Muspelheim. Though you may opt to get both, generally you should consider '''either''' this or [[Fire Wall]] (or neither).
*[[Thunderstorm]]: Rarely taken in place of [[Fire Ball]] or [[Heaven's Drive]], this spell could merit consideration for a dedicated group-focused Sage.
*[[Volcano]]: Alongside [[Deluge]] it is often considered the land spell of choice for parties. You may opt to skip this spell (and its pre-requisite [[Flame Launcher]] 1) if you haven't taken either [[Fire Ball]] or [[Fire Bolt]], '''and''' you are certain you do not want to take it solely for parties or [[Soul Strike]]/[[Heaven's Drive]] usage.
*[[Magic Rod]] A nifty tool that can help with managing annoying spellcasting monsters like Spectring, Frus or Owl Baron. Generally more than 1 point in this skill is not needed, as even rank 1 has generous timing for using it to catch the end of a monster's spell cast.
*[[Dispell]]: Though somewhat niche, it does have some merit as a dump for leftover points as there are some difficult enemies (E.g., Miasmus) and MvPs for which the spell is useful for.

=== Hindsight ===
* STR: 1
* AGI: 88+
* VIT: 1
* INT: 99
* DEX: 9-40
* LUK: 1

No other pure spell caster gets as up close and personal to their foes as the Hindsight (HS) Sage. [[Hindsight]] or ("[[Auto Spell]]") is a buff that allows melee auto attack swings to automatically cast a given spell, depending on the rank of [[Hindsight]] used. HS sages can freely switch between ranks of [[Hindsight]] on the fly, allowing them to react to situations as needed: Suddenly mobbed? Use rank 8 for [[Heaven's Drive]]. Hard hitting foe? Rank 10 will protect you with [[Safety Wall]]. There is no melee build more adaptable than the Hindsight Sage. 

HS sages are usually built one of two ways, either 99 INT 99 AGI or some variation where more DEX is taken at the cost of AGI. 99 INT/AGI HS will have higher flee and ASPD than DEX HS, but DEX HS have faster cast for manual bolts and buffing with [[Energy Coat]]/[[Double Bolt]]. These two builds also differ in terms of playstyle. Higher DEX HS start combat on a target by manually casting a bolt spell (which [[Free Cast]] allows for without interrupting auto attacking) whereas HS sages who go 99 INT/AGI often choose to rely on [[Hindsight]] alone to produce their bolts.

Similar to INT/DEX [[Wizard]]s, Bolt sages try to reach the highest MATK multiplier they can ([[Sage#On INT, MATK Breakpoints & SP Regen]]) while also maximizing DEX. Where Bolter Sage differs from [[Wizard]] is primarily in their choice of headgear, accessories and weapon. Bolt sages make use of accessory/headgear cards which boost the effectiveness of specific [[Mage]] skills, namely: Siroma, Conductring, Shade of Payon and Indignant Soul cards. A Bolt Sage will swap out these equipment slots depending on whether they're using [[Cold Bolt]], [[Lightning Bolt]] or [[Soul Strike]] respectively. Though AGI bolters ideally use the WELDER card, they could also use other +FLEE cards in the garment slot, alongside similar equipment/cards to reach 95% flee on a given monster. 

Where weapons are concerned, Staff of the Scholar is often the most common choice of staff owing to it essentially being a supercharged Evil Bone Wand with its partial MDEF penetration bonus. Whilst in a group with [[Blessing]], bolt sages may aim to reach higher INT MATK breakpoints using Wizardry Staff or the Memory Book combo (Memory Book + Monocle + Pocket Watch). They may also opt to use Rod [4] with Pitman Cards slotted in situations where they'll be making heavy use of [[Heaven's Drive]] or [[Earth Spike]], or Fur Seal Cards should an AGI bolter need the bonus +FLEE. Absent the [[Violent Gale]] buff, sages can make good use of the Wing Staff + Eagle Wing [1] combo for its +20% movement speed increase.

Bolt sages are an excellent choice for a new or budgeting player, as they can still be very effective even absent important accessory cards. Staff of the Scholar, Crown/Tiara, Celebrant's Mitten and Mage Coat are cheap first investments alongside Creamy and Vitata Cards, which are two cards sages have an easy time hunting.

=== Hindsight Gear ===
Hindsight sages value INT, AGI, +FLEE and +MATK equipment. Their weapon of choice is generally a Bible [2]. Legacy of Dragon to reach a higher MATK breakpoint ([[Sage#On INT, MATK Breakpoints & SP Regen]]) are also sometimes used, as are Photo Album [4] with Red Ferus or Pitman cards for [[Fire Ball]] and [[Heaven's Drive]]/[[Earth Spike]] use respectively. 

HS sages can make good use of the [[Corruptor Card]], with some caveats. The first is that sustaining their SP while using [[Corruptor Card]] is very difficult without considerable investment in [[Increase SP Recovery]], especially paired with [[Energy Coat]] or [[Elemental Change]] usage. Another consideration is that although [[Hindsight]] activates regardless of whether you hit a target or not, item procs like [[Corruptor Card]] ''do'' require you to hit a target. Therefore, especially for 9 DEX HS sages, Mummy Cards slotted in a weapon may be necessary for using Corruptor depending on the 100% hit requirement for a given target. 

HS sages are a reasonable option for newer/budgeting players, providing they aim to level one like a bolter sage would for the first 65 or so levels ([[Sage#Hindsight 2]]). Aside from the suggestions listed in the bolter gear section above, a Bible [2] can be purchased from an NPC in the Geffen Mage Guild and the Pantie+Undershirt combo remains a superb budget option for any AGI-based character.

== Sage Leveling ==
=== Bolter ===

''' Recommended Stat Progression '''
* A solid method of building a bolt sage is to dump all your stat points into INT until ~90-99 base INT, followed by DEX (with AGI at some later point if you're flee-based). More INT translates into both higher damage and faster cast times as you're able to downrank your bolt skills more and more while still guaranteeing a one shot on a target (be sure to use the stat calc [[Sage#See Also]]). It also fascilitates the use of the already fast cast [[Soul Strike]] as one of the better options available to sage for leveling in maps like UT2 (see below) as very high MATK is needed to one shot the [[Undead]]/[[Ghost]]s there with [[Double Bolt]].
