=== Hindsight ===

''' Recommended Stat Progression '''
* Hindsight sages have a difficult problem regarding their stat progression. A sage's ability to kill things with [[Hindsight]] relies both on their fire power (INT) and rate of attack (AGI), but unlike other melee characters they have little weapon damage to rely on and INT's contribution to magic damage starts off much slower than STR and ATK. Trying to raise both attributes equally will result in a miserable experience where you kill things slowly whilst also not being able to flee anything. There are two solutions to this problem:
# Pump INT almost exclusively and level in some of the same areas as a bolter sage until the mid 80s - early 90s. The advantage to this method is that it's the fastest and easiest option, but with the downside that you won't ''really'' be playing a Hindsight sage and will have to live as a somewhat gimped bolt sage until the later levels. Following this method you should invest in INT until ~90 base INT such that you can hit 105 INT total at least by job50, though many opt to go all the way to 99 base INT.
# The second option is to put points in only AGI until ~70 AGI, leveling exclusively as a mobber in parties. Generally you would be a mobber in Stala, Medusa or Abyss parties only (see those section in the leveling guide below for details). The obvious disadvantage to this method is that you would be entirely reliant on groups for leveling, but the upside is that you can fight in combat as an actual Hindsight sage sooner than the first solution. HS sages can start "functioning" reasonably well at around ~70 base AGI and 105 total INT. It should also be noted that it is recommended to level as a [[Mage]] built normally until 45 and then stat reset using Pheonix ([[Stat Reset#Full Stat Reset (Base Level 1-45)]]) for any HS sage who opts to do this.

==Gameplay Tips==
====Vertical Fire Wall====
Vertical [[Fire Wall]] is the technique where you cast [[Fire Wall]] adjacent to your character so it casts vertically. This is useful because combined with mobbing and anticipating monster's pathing route, you can have monsters hit all 3 pillars of fire.

<center>[[File:Firewall02.jpg|550px]]</center>
<center>''Cast [[Fire Wall]] on the yellow circle while anticipating for monsters' movements in the red arrow direction.<ref name=":0">http://myrolife.blogspot.com/2016/05/verticle-fire-wall-guide.html</ref>'' </center>


<center>[[File:Firewall03.jpg|500px]]</center>
<center>''Monsters will moving in the red arrow direction, hitting all cells of the [[Fire Wall]].<ref name=":0" />''</center>

For a more in-depth guide on vertical [[Fire Wall]]s, read [http://myrolife.blogspot.com/2016/05/verticle-fire-wall-guide.html Vertical Fire Wall Guide]

===On INT, MATK Breakpoints & SP Regen===
MATK before gear and other modifiers is calculated by this formula: Min MATK = (INT + [INT / 7]^2) ~ Max MATK = (INT + [INT / 5]^2), where INT is rounded down each time.

This MATK is then modified by gear effects like +15% from most Staves and set bonuses like Survivor's and Pocket Watch combo.

So INT scales MATK and thus damage quadratically in increments of 5 and 7. It also increases Max SP and SP Regen by 1% of Base SP every INT and 1 point per tick every 6 INT respectively. The increased Max SP also increases SP Regen by 1 for every 100 total Max SP. Once you reach 120 INT there is a further SP Regen increase by 1 point every 2 INT above 112 INT, so 4 right away and 1 every 2 INT from then on. 

Both Bolter and Hindsight sages generally aim to reach 120 total INT when solo. In groups, with [[Blessing]] they may aim for 133 or 135 INT total, depending on whether they need elemental armor cards or would have to sacrifice accessory cards.

== Hit versus Accuracy ==
Sonic Acceleration does not give a flat +50 [[Hit]]. If your status window Hit is 100, using [[Sonic Blow]] while having SA will not increase it to 150. SA gives +50% "Hit", the Hit actually being Accuracy rate. Accuracy rate is the final percentage the game calculates after counting in the player's Hit Rate and Enemy's Flee Rate. If the player's Hit was 100 and the enemy's Flee is 150, the Accuracy rate is 30%. When the player uses Sonic Blow, Sonic Acceleration increases that 30% chance to 45%.

The '''Soul Harvest''' skill allows the [[Super Novice]] to sometimes find a '''Soul Fragment''' when killing non-boss monsters.

== Soul Fragments ==
A primary use of the Soul Fragments is to '''reset the death counter via the Orb of Life''' on the Death Reset map. Each reset costs '''150 Soul Fragments'''.

Soul Fragments are '''Account Bound.''' They can be shared among characters in the same account via Kafra Storage, but cannot be traded, put in Guild Storage, sold on Vend, or sent via RODEX.

The other use for Soul Fragments is to buy Novice-specific gears, available via the '''Dimensional Servant''' on the Death Reset map.

{{Skill Info | class = Thief | class2 = Super Novice | class3 = | type = Active | levels = 10 (Fixed) | prereqs = None | quest = | spcost = 10 | hpcost = | time = None | delay = 1 second | duration = | target = Monsters | range = Melee | area = | knock = | element = | status = | catalyst = | cf_name = | cf_value = }} == Description == Attempts to "steal" an item from the targeted [[monster]]. Only items dropped by the monster can be stolen. A successful attempt will not affect what is dropped when the monster dies. After success, it is not possible to Steal again from the same monster. [[Boss]]-protocol monsters cannot be stolen from. Cards can never be stolen. === How Steal Works === Each monster has their own drop table. As an example: {| class="wikitable" |+ !Item !Drop Ratio |- |Skull |70% |- |Brigan |70% |- |Oridecon |30% |- |Elunium |30% |- |Chain Mail |25% |- |Silk Robe |25% |- |Elemental Sword |0.02% |} When Steal is triggered, a roll happens sequentially from top-down. For each item, if the attempt fails, a subsequent roll will happen for the next item on the table. The ramification for this is that if you want to steal higher rarity items like Elemental Sword in the example above, you will have to fail Steal attempt rolls on all the items prior to it on the drop table. The formula for stealing is: 
(playerDEX - mobDEX)/2 + ((stealLvl * 6) + 4)
You can think of the steal "success chance" as more of a rate modifier. For example, for a player with steal 10 and 71 dex vs Kapha with 73 dex... 
(71 - 73)/2 + (10*6) + 4) 
-1 + 64 = 63%.
You then times the drop rate by that: Yellow plate 65.01 * 0.63 = 41% chance to steal. Success = steal and finish, fail = check next item. {| class="wikitable" !Skill Level || Success Chance |- |1 || 10% |- |2 || 16% |- |3 || 22% |- |4 || 28% |- |5 || 34% |- |6 || 40% |- |7 || 46% |- |8 || 52% |- |9 || 58% |- |10 || 64% |} == See Also == * [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1GXbyv8D3TPf0w6O3TVwMn09FmJO9JJW0raC49jXDUis/edit?gid=0#gid=0 Steal % by DEX for notable monsters spreadsheet] * https://tools.payonstories.com/steal {{Navbox Thief}} {{Navbox SuperNovice}}

__TOC__ {{Infobox Job|jobBase=Novice|jobName=Super Novice|jobType=Novice|changesAt=[[Al De Baran]]|skills=49|skillPoints=419|questSkills=0 |str=5|agi=5|vit=5|int=5|dex=5|luk=5}} ==About Super Novices== Super novices are a special kind of class which exploits nearly every first class skill. Super Novices also sport highly effective armor and shields which reduce elemental attacks. Super Novices are the most versatile among all classes have "true freedom" in build and skills. The downside to this freedom of skills is the limitations that haunt all Novices -- very low HP and SP (a Novice at heart). Super Novices lose the use of the Play Dead skill and also lose exp upon death with 1 HP remaining, just like a regular first class. Super Novices only can equip anything a normal Novice would be able to, including specialized Novice only equipment. Super Novices also have a Job Level of 99. Additionally, Super Novices have their own unique cart, should they choose to get one. ==Jobchange Guide== {{:Super Novice Job Change Guide}} ==Builds== ===Caster=== * STR: 1 * AGI: 1 * VIT: 1-40 * INT: 90+ * DEX: 90+ * LUK: 1 The only class that currently has the ability to achieve instant cast (150 DEX), a caster Super Novice is an incredibly efficient farmer that can be tailored to your needs with very few downsides. Compared to other casters, they do much higher damage as a result of INT bonuses and the Hypnotist Staff giving +25% MATK (instead of the regular 15%), but this comes at the cost of having much lower maximum SP even with the bonus granted by the Angelic set. They may also struggle on higher end maps due to their squishiness, but even that can be mitigated depending on your build. Super Novice remains to be explored by many adventurers. Here are the secrets of Super Novicehood. :Doridori ::Using the command "/doridori" restore HP/SP two times faster. You need to shake your head approximately 6 times in a 1.5-3s time period. A super novice insists that head-shaking supposedly speeds up his SP restoration. This only applies to HP and SP recovered by the skills Increase HP Recovery & Increase SP Recovery (Despite the description on the international version website, this only affects SP recovery, not HP recovery at all) :Guardian Angel ::A Super Novice has its own level up Angel. When leveling-up, this Guardian Angel is different from those of the other classes. The angel will cast all skills from the following list: Kyrie Eleison, Magnificat, Gloria, Suffragium and Impositio Manus on the Super Novice. :Never give up! ::According to hearsay, when a Super Novice's HP reaches 0 when he she is 99.0%-99.9%, their Guardian Angel may appear to refill his HP and cast Mental Strength on the Super Novice. This will not occur again until you relog or level another level. :Undying Love ::A Super Novice wife will give +1 for every stat when she uses the marriage skill Undying Love on her husband. Also, the husband's SP recovery will double. However, the wife's Stats will all be reduced by 1. This however only occurs randomly and temporarily. :The Power of love ::A super novice wife will heal her husband for 2x the normal amount. :Really Super ::If a Super Novice can manage to avoid even a single death until job 70 and onwards, you will get +10 for all stats. If you die anytime afterwards, you will lose that bonus. This death record can be cleared (and the bonus stats recovered) using Super Novice Spirit. :Super Novice Cart ::Super Novices get their own special cart for an extra fee (1900z) in Al De Baran behind the Kafra Headquarters in the Northwestern corner of the map. :Fury ::A strange phenomenon when the Super Novice's EXP reaches increments of 10% such as, at 10.0%, 20.0% - 80.0%, 90.0%. During these times the Super Novice has been rumored to summon his Guardian Angel for help. If you change maps or relog, you have to repeat all the steps but otherwise you can just repeat the last 3 lines to get fury status again. Type 7 lines of text (or you will be silenced) and then type the following phrase to get the Fury Status (critical rate +50): ::* Dear angel, can you hear my voice? ::* I am (your name) Super Novice~ ::* Help me out~ Please~ T_T ::* & (Edit 01/2024: In PayonStories one line above is changed. The original line is "... SuperNovice~") ::OR ::* Guardian Angel, can you hear my voice? ^^; ::* My name is (your name), and I'm a Super Novice~ ::* Please help me~ T.T ::* & ::& is random text. Sometimes you don't have write one more line after "Help me out" to make the effect activate. ==Super Novice: Life After 99== Upon reaching level 99, a super novice has a few new tricks up its sleeves. *The two Super Novice Secrets which depend on your current % of Base EXP can still be used, but you must continue leveling to gain the exp required. :*To Fury, you must gain n*10.0x million exp (where n=1,2,3,...). :*In order to use Mental Strength you must gain an additional 99 million exp or more after 99-ing. :*Upon attaining 99,999,999 exp (as shown on the character select screen) you will be able to use both the novice fury chant and Mental Strength upon 0 hp. ==Super Novice Data== ===Payon Stories Balance Changes=== *[[Soul Harvest]] (Quest Skill) added, which allows a Super Novice to obtain Soul Fragments- a currency used to reset their death counter and buy Novice-specific gear (see the skill page for a complete list). *HP Changes: Super Novices will now receive bonus HP at every 10 level increments starting at level 40. ==Overview==

[[Image:Swordman.jpeg|thumb|left]]

Natural born leaders and men-at-arms, swordman are the frontline of any adventuring party. 

Swordman are capable tanks and mobbers, owing to their ability to equip heavier armor and access to skills like [[Provoke]] and [[Endure]]. Swordman are also capable of wielding a greater variety of weapon types than any other 1st job, and have powerful physical attacks in the form of [[Bash]] and [[Magnum Break]].

Upon reaching job lvl 40, swordman can swear to uphold the codes of chivalry as [[Knight]]s, or take sacred vows and prepare for the holy war as [[Crusader]]s. 

==Jobchange Guide==
See [[Swordman Job Change Guide]] for more information.










== Swordman Builds ==
To make sure your Swordman becomes fully functional, you’ve got to plan your stat build according to the 2nd job you’ll graduate as. This section details how you should allocate your stats until you job change. You can see the final stats allocation for the various builds on the [[Knight]] and [[Crusader]] pages. 

Swordman have these most common builds to evolve into:

=== SVD Knight ===
'''S'''trength, '''V'''itality, '''D'''exterity knights or "SVD" knights are the premiere brawlers in the game. Capable of tanking hoards of enemies with their very high health pools whilst simultaneously dispatching them with [[Brandish Spear]] or [[Bowling Bash]]. SVD is a choice of build for aspiring knights who want to level up as fast and as efficiently as possible, or who relish the idea of being an unstoppable behemoth.

'''Stat distribution :'''
* Raise DEX and VIT together until you reach 30-35 DEX, then focus entirely on STR. You want to prioritise STR because your leveling speed/efficiency later on depends on minimizing how many [[Pierce]], [[Bowling Bash]] or [[Brandish Spear]]s you need to kill a target or group of targets.

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Helm, Iron Cain
* Body: Chain Mail[0], Full Plate[0]
* Weapon: Damascus[0], VVS [[Blacksmith]]-forged elemental Lance
* Offhand: Shield[0]
* Garment: Manteau[0]
* Shoes: Boots[0], Greaves[0]
* Accessories: Matyr Leash, Ring [0]

<u>First Major Investments:</u> VVS [[Blacksmith]]-forged elemental Lance, Pike [4] (Orc Lady Card x 3, Hydra Card), Shield/Buckler[1] (Thara Frog Card)

=== AGI (2h) Knight ===
For knights who prefer the sword over the spear, or for those who like the more leisurely style of autoattacking enemies. A 2h knight's playstyle is a mix of quickly going from enemy to enemy and gathering groups of foes and knocking them over with [[Bowling Bash]]. Sharing the title with Spear Saders, 2h knights are the fastest autoattackers in the game, capable of reaching more than 185 ASPD (5+ attacks per second).

'''Stat distribution :'''
* Raise DEX and AGI together until you reach 30-35 DEX, then focus on AGI. Around 60-70 AGI, start investing in STR. Those who are more geared/wealthy can prioritize STR earlier and more-so to capitalize on carded weaponry and +flee equipment.

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Helm, Iron Cain, Sakkat
* Body: Pantie, Chain Mail[0], Full Plate [0]
* Weapon: Claymore[0], Two-Handed Sword[0], VVS [[Blacksmith]]-forged elemental Claymore
* Offhand: NPC-bought Shield [0]
* Garment: Undershirt, Manteau[0]
* Shoes: Boots[0], Greaves[0]
* Accessories: Matyr Leash, Ring [0]

<u>First Major Investments:</u> VVS [[Blacksmith]]-forged elemental Claymore, Two-Handed Sword[2] (Goblin Card x 2)

===  GC (Grand Cross) ===
For Crusaders who want to combine might with magic, GC saders are armor-clad spellcasters who specialize in killing groups of [[Undead]] and [[Shadow]] element enemies with their [[Grand Cross]] spell. Though more of a late bloomer than other types of crusaders, GC saders eventually make themselves rich as they rid the world of evil with maps like Glast Heim Chivalry and Niflheim as their stomping grounds.

For more information see: [[Crusader#GC (Grand Cross)]]

'''Stat distribution :'''
* Levels 1 - 45: You should follow the stat distribution for AGI (2h) Knight/AGI Spear until level 45, and then respec to the proper stats by talking to Pheonix (See: [[Stat_Reset#Overview]]).
* Level 46 - 60: After respeccing, you should have primarily invested in INT, with a little bit of VIT and DEX (E.g., 80 INT, 30 VIT, 20 DEX).

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Helm, Iron Cain
* Body: Chain Mail[0], Full Plate [0]
* Weapon: Haedonggum[0], Fireblend*
* Offhand: Mirror Shield [0]
* Garment: Manteau[0], Ragamuffin Manteau
* Shoes: Boots[0], Greaves[0]
* Accessories: Earring

<u>First Major Investments:</u> Fireblend (as an early leveling tool only, to be later resold), Mirror Shield [1] (Thara Frog Card), Earring[0], Diadem of the High Priestess [1] (Elder Willow Card)

=== HC (Holy Cross) ===
For those that like flashy skills, or who fancy themselves as [[Demon]] hunters. HC saders are similar to GC saders in that they primarily hunt [[Shadow]] and [[Undead]] element foes, but differ in that they do so with spears rather than spells. These crusaders are skill spammers, making use of the incredibly efficient ranged physical skill [[Holy Cross]] to kill monsters.   

For more information see: [[Crusader#HC (Holy Cross)]]

'''Stat distribution :'''
* Levels 1 - 45: You should follow the stat distribution for AGI (2h) Knight/AGI Spear until level 45, and then respec to the proper stats by talking to Pheonix (See: [[Stat_Reset#Overview]]).
* Level 46 - 60: After respeccing, you should have primarily invested in STR, with a little bit in INT and AGI (E.g., 80 STR, 30 INT, 20 AGI).

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>

<u>First Major Investments:</u> Trident [3] (Santa Poring Card x 3)

=== AGI Spear ===
For crusaders who want to hunt more than just [[Demon]]s or [[Undead]], AGI Spear or "Spear Saders" have almost total freedom as to where they can go with their collection of two-handed spears. They are similar to AGI knights in that they are the fastest autoattackers in the game, but differ by trading AoE capability for higher single target kill speed.

For more information see: [[Crusader#AGI Spear]]

'''Stat distribution :'''
* Raise DEX and AGI together until you reach 30-35 DEX, then focus on AGI. Around 70-80 AGI, start investing in STR. Those who are more geared/wealthy can prioritize STR earlier and more-so to capitalize on carded weaponry and +flee equipment.

'''Equipment'''

=== Boomer (Shield Boomerang) ===
Utterly unique, Shield Boomerang Crusaders or "boomers" turn their defense into offense by quite literally throwing their shields at their foes. Boomers combine their ability to rapidly dispatch low - medium health enemies with their mounted movement speed and hardiness to be one of the most efficient farmers around.  

For more information see: [[Crusader#Boomer (Shield Boomerang)]]

'''Stat distribution :'''
* Levels 1 - 45: You should follow the stat distribution for AGI (2h) Knight/AGI Spear until level 45, and then respec to the proper stats by talking to Pheonix (See: [[Stat_Reset#Overview]]).
* Level 46 - 60: After respeccing, you should have primarily invested in STR, with a little bit in INT and VIT (E.g., 80 STR, 30 INT, 20 VIT).

=== Devo (Devotion) ===
These crusaders focus on maximizing the defensive and protective potential of their vocation. Either as a tank, mobber or through their special role of keeping party members alive with [[Sacrifice]], Devo Saders make for an essential component of parties. Devo crusaders can be either full support, hybrid boomer or hybrid gc crusaders.

For more information see: [[Crusader#Devo (Devotion)]]

'''Stat distribution :'''
* Levels 1 - 45: You should follow the stat distribution for AGI (2h) Knight/AGI Spear until level 45, and then respec to the proper stats by talking to Pheonix (See: [[Stat_Reset#Overview]]).
* Level 46 - 60: After respeccing, you should have primarily invested in VIT if you're planning on being a full support Devo Sader. Otherwise, how you invest your stats will depend on whether you're going to be a hybrid boomer or hybrid gc devo sader (see those build sections) with an added priority on VIT.

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Helm, Iron Cain
* Body: Chain Mail[0], Full Plate [0]
* Weapon: Damascus[0]
* Offhand: Shield[0]
* Garment: Manteau[0]
* Shoes: Boots[0], Greaves[0]
* Accessories: Necklace, Clip [1] (Spore Card)

<u>First Major Investments:</u>: Buying high defense Swordman--only armor like Full Plate[0] and Greaves[0] from NPCs and upgrading them to the safe limit (+4) with elunium is a solid first investment to make you a more solid mobber and tank for parties.

=== Devo (Devotion) ===

An aspiring full support Devo sader should build their attributes and level on the same monsters as an 2h Knight/AGI sader would until level 45, and then reset their stats as appropriate (i.e., VIT) by talking to Pheonix (See: Stat_Reset). Solo leveling after this point is largely impractical, and the devo sader should try and find groups where they can serve as the party's mobber for their leveling needs (e.g., Mi Gao -> Stala/Pront Guild Dungeon/Turtle Dungeon -> Magma/Abyss).

A devo sader built as a hybrid boomer or GC sader should follow those leveling sections above. 

==Class Data==

===Payon Stories Balance Changes===
See [[Class Rebalance#Swordman|Class Rebalance (Swordman)]] for detailed information.
*[[HP Recovery|'''HP Recovery''']]: Ticks every 5 Seconds in line with the overall increased HP/SP regen in Payon Stories.
*[[Bash|'''Bash''']]: SP cost has been reduced to a rate of 3 SP + 1 SP per skill level.
*[[Magnum Break|'''Magnum Break''']]: Range has been increased to 4 cells, its SP cost has been reduced from 30 SP to 18 SP per cast.
*[[Moving HP Recovery|'''Moving HP Recovery''']]: Can now be learned at Job Level 15. The quest now requires [[Image:713.png|24px|]] 50 [https://cp.payonstories.com/?module=item&action=view&id=713 Empty Bottle] instead of 200.
*[[Sword Mastery| '''Sword Mastery''']] and [[Two-Handed Sword Mastery| '''Two-Handed Sword Mastery''']]: Have been combined into [[Blade Mastery]].

1. In Izlude, enter the Swordman Guild on the west side of town ''(izlude 52, 138)''. Talk to the Swordman NPC in the center room behind the desk ''(izlude_in 74, 172)'', then the guard to the west. This guard will transfer you to a new room.

2. Talk to the guard named '''Test Hall Staff''' in the room to initiate the test. You have '''10 minutes''' to complete the test.

3. ''First Map'': A simple map. Just walk to the other side. If you fall you will be sent back to the beginning.

4. ''Second Map'': This map involves two parallel bridges. Take your time and be careful not to fall off. You don't have to hold the mouse button down to walk.

5. ''Third Map'': Similar to the first map except for the upper and lower levels. The lower level has a darker color than the upper level. Take your time and click carefully to get to the lower level. At the point where there is a gap in the top level, simply click on the lower level, and you will jump down. Then do the same to get back up.

6. Upon traversing the three maps and their checkpoints, talk to '''Mae''' in the last room to finish the test.

7. After exiting the test maps, speak to the large Swordman in the main room to become a [[Swordman]].

==Overview==

[[Image: Thief.jpg|thumb|left]]

''Carpe diem'' -- Seize the day! A motto that perfectly captures the spirit of thieves. Wielding dagger or bow, they strike swiftly, overwhelming foes with [[Double Attack]]s. Their high flee thanks to [[Improve Dodge]] makes them difficult to hit, while skills like [[Hiding]], [[Envenom]] and [[Steal]] add a layer of thematic utility that makes them truly feel unique. 

Thieves are a job with a high level of accessibility thanks to their highly practical passive skills, which makes them a popular choice for new players and veterans alike. 

Upon reaching job lvl 40, thieves can choose to undertake a trial to join the mysterious [[Assassin]]s, or embrace a life of greater crime and cunning by becoming a [[Rogue]].

==Jobchange Guide==
See [[Thief Job Change Guide]] for more information.














== Thief Builds ==
To make sure your thief becomes fully functional, you’ve got to plan your stat build according to the 2nd job you’ll graduate as. This section details different [[Rogue]] and [[Assassin]] builds and how you should allocate your stats until you job change. You can see the final stats allocation for the various builds on the [[Rogue]] and [[Assassin]] pages. 

All thieves (regardless of 2nd class) should distribute their skill point as follows:

* [[Double Attack]] 10
* [[Improve Dodge]] 10
* [[Envenom]] 3
* [[Detoxify]] 1
* [[Envenom]] 10
* [[Steal]] 10
* [[Hiding]] 8

If planning on job changing ''before'' job50, the above distribution can be changed, but this is not recommended. The jEXP requirements for 1st classes has been modified on Payon Stories to be lower, and whether changing into an [[Assassin]] or a [[Rogue]], a valuable Gladius [3] is awarded if changing at job50 thief.

Thieves have these most common builds to evolve into:

=== Dual dagger(DD)/Hybrid Katar Assassin ===
DD assassins make use of their unique ability to equip two daggers at once, allowing them to reach the pinnacle of single target DPS. They also boast excellent mobbing ability thanks to the very powerful [[Venom Splasher]] poison skill. Another version of this build uses Sidewinder carded Katars and forgoes [[Venom Splasher]] to instead get [[Katar Mastery]] and [[Grimtooth]], allowing for an alternate playstyle (usually differing only in terms of skills taken, not stat allocation).

* '''Pros''' : Excellent mobbing ability, highest dps on low defense monsters, good mobber in static parties.
* '''Cons''' : Notorious for being "The most expensive build in the game" (huge arsenal of carded gladius/main gauche)

'''Stat distribution :'''
Raise DEX and AGI together until you reach 20-30 DEX, then focus on AGI. Around 40-50 AGI, start investing in and prioritizing STR (STR should generally be 20-30 points higher than AGI). Those who are more geared/wealthy can prioritize STR over AGI much earlier instead. 

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Sakkat
* Body: Pantie
* Weapon: NPC-bought Damascus, Poring Dagger
* Offhand: NPC-bought Buckler [0]
* Garment: Undershirt
* Shoes: NPC-bought Boots [0]
* Accessories: Matyr Leash

<u>First Major Investments:</u>
* Ranked VVS Wind/Fire Damascus, Brooch [0], Sidewinder carded Jamadhar [1] (if going hybrid katar)

=== Critical Assassin ===
Critical Assassins use of the special assassin-only Katar weapon class to double their critical rate, allowing them to dispatch high DEF/Flee enemies that many other classes struggle with. These assassins also boast high single target DPS, have excellent one-shot potential with [[Sonic Blow]] and strong mobbing potential with [[Grimtooth]].

* '''Pros''' : Affordable low-end equipment, critical hits bypass DEF/Flee making them excellent hunters of those enemies, can fill in for ABB [[Hunter]] role in parties, good mobber, the sound of rapid critical hits is pure dopamine 
* '''Cons''' : High-end equipment is extremely expensive

'''Stat distribution :'''

*Levels 1 - 45: It's best to just build your thief like an aspiring Gank Rogue (see below) until base level 45, and then respec to the proper stats by talking to Pheonix (See: [[Stat_Reset#Overview]])
*Levels 45 - 60+: You shouldn't invest in LUK at all until becoming an [[Assassin]], as you'll get little out of it. Focus solely on AGI/STR, usually more AGI than STR (~10-20 point difference).

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Sakkat
* Body: Pantie
* Weapon: NPC-bought Damascus, Poring Dagger
* Offhand: NPC-bought Buckler [0]
* Garment: Undershirt
* Shoes: NPC-bought Boots [0]
* Accessories: Matyr Leash

<u>First Major Investments:</u>
* Skeleton Soldier/Bonechewer carded Jur [3], Kobold carded Clip [1], Ruby Pumps, Yoyo Pet

=== Gank/Snatcher Rogue ===
[[Snatcher]] is a unique skill that can proc the [[Steal]] skill when you auto-attack a monster without consuming SP. These rogues in essence get double the loot from each monster confronted. A Gank Rogue is built to capitalize on this skill, making for not only an excellent farmer but a character with great self-sustain and map variety.

* '''Pros''' : More loot means more money, relatively cheap to make, excellent sustain and flexibility thanks to [[Plagiarism]]
* '''Cons''' : Not very good in non-static parties, eventually becomes an inferior farmer of low HP enemies compared to other jobs who can more efficiently one shot them.

'''Stat distribution :'''

Raise DEX and AGI together until you reach 30-40 DEX, then focus on AGI. Around 50-60 AGI, start investing in STR (STR should generally be ~20 points lower than AGI). Those who are more geared/wealthy can prioritize STR over AGI instead.

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Sakkat
* Body: Pantie
* Weapon: NPC-bought Damascus, Poring Dagger
* Offhand: NPC-bought Buckler [0]
* Garment: Undershirt
* Shoes: NPC-bought Boots [0]
* Accessories: Matyr Leash

<u>First Major Investments:</u>
* Ranked VVS Wind/Fire Damascus, Brooch [0], Myst Case Carded Hat [1]/Cap [1]/Marionette Doll [1], Creamy Carded Clip [1]

=== Bow Rogue (AGI) ===
Bow Rogues can be thought of as a more flexible [[Hunter]]. While they may boast less raw power when wielding a bow, these rogues have the added ability to copy almost any player skill with [[Plagiarism]], allowing them to do things [[Hunter]]s can't like mob groups of enemies with [[Bowling Bash]] or dispatch high DEF foes with [[Acid Terror]].

* '''Pros''' : Relatively cheap to make, can function similarly to Gank Rogue with the same benefits (especially using Great Snake card), ranged character with those inherit benefits to kill speed/lower damage received
* '''Cons''' : Thief leveling with only a 3 cell bow range can be painful, without [[Arrow Crafting]] must rely on another character to create quivers/craft arrows.

'''Stat distribution :''' DEX should always be ~20 points ahead of AGI, it is still the most important stat for AGI Bow Rogues. Avoid investing in INT (if at all) until late levels as a [[Rogue]].

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Sakkat
* Body: Pantie
* Weapon: NPC-bought Gakkung [1]/Repeating Crossbow [1]
* Offhand: NPC-bought Buckler [0]
* Garment: Undershirt
* Shoes: NPC-bought Boots [0]
* Accessories: Matyr Leash

<u>First Major Investments:</u>
* Sidewinder carded Gakkung [2] ''or'' Sidewinder carded Repeating Crossbow [1], Apple of Archer, Glove [0], Brooch [0]

=== Bow/Caster Rogue (INT) ===
INT Rogue is a build that allows a player to be especially creative with their use of [[Plagiarism]]. Because of how bow damage is calculated, these rogues have an unusual combination of high ATK, fast cast time and a high MATK/SP recovery which let them make use of skills other rogues would not, like [[Grand Cross]], [[Blaze Shield]], [[Storm Gust]], and more.

* '''Pros''' : Unique (dazzle others with your weirdness), can fill wizard roles in parties at high levels, has access to a super-powered version of [[Water Ball]], better at using [[Acid Terror]] than [[Alchemist]]s, no one will ever be as cool as you.
* '''Cons''' : Early-mid [[Rogue]] leveling will be painful, leveling experience will be a struggle without very careful planning of maps and skills to plagerise.

'''Stat distribution :'''

*Levels 1 - 45: It's best to just build your thief like an aspiring Bow Rogue (AGI) (see above) until base level 45, and then respec to the proper stats by talking to Pheonix (See: [[Stat_Reset#Overview]])
*Levels 45 - 60+: Largely depends on how you plan on leveling as a [[Rogue]]. If you plan on leveling with spells like [[Blaze Shield]] (currently bugged for [[Plagiarism]]) then pump only INT and rely on Mi Gao parties (see below) until you can use Plagiarism 10. For most builds, DEX will be by and large the priority and should be ~30-40 points higher than INT, or raised exclusively until reaching 8x/9x DEX.

'''Equipment'''

<u>Beginner:</u>
* Head: Sakkat
* Body: Pantie
* Weapon: NPC-bought Gakkung [1]/Repeating Crossbow [1]
* Offhand: 
* Garment: Undershirt
* Shoes: NPC-bought Boots [0]
* Accessories: Matyr Leash

<u>First Major Investments:</u>
* Andre/Zipper Bear carded Gakkung [2], FUEL carded Boots [1], Apple of Archer, Glove [0]

== Thief Leveling ==
The following is a list of suggested leveling areas for each build based on stat/build assumptions detailed above.

1. Head off to the Pyramids, which is north-west of [[Morroc]].  

2. At the pyramid (58,159), enter, and head for the middle of the map to the Thief Guild (90,105).

3. Once inside, follow the hallway down and take the left gate (90,115). In here you will see two NPCs that will guide you through the quest. 

4. Talk to the one closest to the portal. She will ask you a few questions, then instruct you to find an "Irrelevant Man" somewhere outside the Pyramid (141, 125) in order to steal mushrooms from a nearby mushroom farm.

[[Image:Thiefmap.JPG]]

5. At the farm, kill the mushrooms and collect the mushrooms that drop.  Aggressive Fabres and Chonchons (and Spores, but they're not aggresive) protect the farm, so you may want to avoid them.  Your mission is to collect at least mushrooms worth of 25 points.

*'''Note''': If you die, you can talk to Mr. Irrelevant to return to the farm as many times as needed. 

6. After collecting a sufficient amount of Mushrooms, head back to Thief Guild.

7. Talk to NPC farthest from the warp portal. He will count your mushrooms and if you have enough points, he will promote you to a Thief.

== Notes ==

Throw Shuriken functions as both a skill and a regular attack, with the following properties:
* It is affected by ATK, +%ATK cards, weapon status cards like Magnolia Cards, STR and weapon damage in the same way most skills are (e.g., [[Haze Slasher]]).
* It does ''not'' benefit from non-weapon cards which have a chance of activating on regular attacks (auto attacks) like [[Corruptor Card]], Enchanted Peach Tree Card, etc.
* This attack inherits both the attack speed and the size penalties of the weapon class you are using. For example, holding a dagger will make you throw faster than holding a huuma shuriken, but will have a 50% penalty VS large enemies whereas the huuma shuriken deals its full damage (see: [[Size]]).

* Activating the skill initiates auto attacking. Knockback from [[Cicada Skin Shed]] is considered a "skill activation" and will cancel the auto attack until re-initiated. 
* The damage dealt by this skill is increased by using shurikens with higher ATK. However, similar to other ammunition like arrows, the actual damage contributed from shuriken ammo +ATK is only a fraction of the displayed value. 
* Throw Shuriken cannot be used while silenced.

==Overview==

[[Image: Wizard.jpg|thumb|left]]

Flashy and powerful, a wizard is the embodiment of the destructive potential of magic.

In terms of solo play, the wizard playstyle is utterly unique compared to other classes. Rather than repeatedly swinging a weapon or spamming a single skill, wizards rely on the tactical use of spells like [[Fire Wall]], [[Ice Wall]] and [[Fire Pillar]] to setup their slow and heavy hitting spells. The likes of [[Storm Gust]] and [[Lord of Vermilion]], when used properly, can decimate entire fields of enemies with their enormous area of effect. 

Alongside [[Priest]]s and [[Bard]]s, wizards are one of the main trio of classes that form the core of most parties in the game. Parties rely on wizards as a perpetual source of damage, able to constantly supply AoE without ever having to worry about them running out of arrows or needing to sit to recover SP. 

==Jobchange Guide==
''See [[Wizard Job Change Guide]] for detailed information.''
















==Builds==
===PvE (DEX)===
*STR: 1
*AGI: 1+
*VIT: 1+
*INT: 99
*DEX: 99
*LUK: 1

The spellcaster who is focused entirely on maximizing their destructive potential build themselves as the ever popular PvE DEX wizard. Many of the most powerful wizard spells have very long cast times (upwards of '''15.5 seconds''') and so the class gets enormous value out of the DEX attribute ([[Wizard#On Dex & Instant Cast]]). DEX wizards rely primarily on their capacity for rifling off rapid spells to protect themselves rather than their sturdiness or evasiveness via VIT and AGI. 

Typically DEX wizards invest 99 points into INT/DEX, however the exact amount may differ by a few points depending on planned equipment and available funds ([[Wizard#PvE (DEX) 2]]). Although similar in terms of stat spread, DEX wizards differ greatly in terms of skill build depending on whether they aim to be more group, MvP or solo focused.

{| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"
|+ class="nowrap" | Skill Overview
|
<center>''The following covers skills that may not be straight forward picks, and provides context to help aspiring DEX wizards make decisions regarding their build.''</center>


*[[Fire Pillar]]: For the most part a solo tool, fire pillar combined with vertical [[Fire Wall]] makes for a potent [[Fire]] damage AoE combination. For "Z Ice Prison" and similar [[Ice Wall]] techniques, only 1 rank of this skill is necessary.
*[[Sightrasher]]: In many ways similar to [[Fire Ball]] as a fast cast AoE [[Fire]] spell. A wizard intent on maxing one of these probably should not get both. Lower ranks (1-2) are sufficient for the purpose of clearing one's [[Ice Wall]], as it has the special property of damaging those walls (Allowing for greater control).
*[[Meteor Storm]]: Typically only taken by group-focused wizards. Unlike [[Storm Gust]] and [[Lord of Vermilion]] where enemies can only be hit by one instance of the spell at a time, multiple [[Meteor Storm]]s can stack. This is why some wizards take the skill for group or MvP content where they are certain to be within [[A Poem of Bragi]] or alongside another wizard.
*[[Lord of Vermilion]]: Its cast time ''decreases'' with higher ranks, rather than what is typical for most spells. With its boost in power, it is rare that this skill gets skipped by any type of wizard. A very high DEX wizard could conceivably take only 1 point in this skill just to use it to break [[Storm Gust]]'s [[Freeze]] if they really wanted to (The difference in cast time between LoV10 and LoV1 is only ~0.5 seconds while in [[A Poem of Bragi]] with high DEX).
*[[Water Ball]]: Typically a very niche spell usable in specific maps only (E.g., Stings in GH Sewers), it is a more justifiable pick for a wizard who intends on grouping or duoing with [[Sage]]s thanks to their [[Deluge]] spell, just keep in mind you need to be in the center of the water in order to get all 25 hits out of the spell.
*[[Quagmire]]: Typically only taken at 2-3 points for its slowing effect as a 10-15 second duration is sufficient for most group or solo purposes. 5 points can be invested for group utility to help reduce damage taken by the tank.
*[[Ice Wall]]: Usually taken for solo use ([[Wizard#Ice Wall Trapping]]) and MvP purposes. Some wizards also take this skill to protect party members in a pinch and for special party setups where the wizard isolates themselves and/or others from enemies. Rank 3 is generally seen as the bare minimum for anyone taking the skill, but will limit its utility to fairly basic use. Rank 5-7 is a more common for solo use, with higher ranks giving more leeway (especially at lower DEX values) for techniques. Up to rank 10 can be taken for MvP purposes, with downranking always being an option if lower durations are needed.
*[[Frost Nova]]: A useful solo skill at early levels, also useful in parties where you don't have a [[Bard]] or [[A Poem of Bragi]]. A party-focused wizard will generally skip this skill, but it does have some merit in debuffing groups/MvPs with its -10 DEX debuff.
*[[Increase SP Recovery]]: Often thought of as irrelevant for wizards and their massive SP pool and INT totals, this skill can be useful in group situations spamming AoE (e.g., Meteor Storm) while in [[A Poem of Bragi]], rare builds who rely on heavy [[Fire Pillar]] usage and in maintaining maximum damage reduction via the [[Energy Coat]] skill in any situation. 
*[[Safety Wall]]: DEX wizards will generally only take this for solo MvP, or supporting others in Endless Tower and other especially difficult maps. The skill is taken at rank 7 (for max cast time reduction) or higher, if it is taken at all.
*[[Frost Diver]]: A more potent defensive tool when using the Frozen Thunder [1] staff or standing in a [[Sage]]'s [[Deluge]]. This skill is more useful in early-mid levels for emergency defense than later on when a rapid [[Storm Gust]] 1 or other spells can be brought out with higher DEX. If you intend on getting [[Frost Nova]], it is pretty much mandatory to max out this skill.
*[[Fire Wall]]: A handy defensive tool but also something used for setup in [[Ice Wall]] mobbing ([[Wizard#Ice Wall Trapping]]), soloing specific MvPs and dealing high damage per second to [[Undead]] and boss protocol enemies. If you intend on taking [[Fire Pillar]], you should max this skill. A wizard who plans on using fire wall should see to mastering the vertical Fire Wall technique ([[Wizard#Vertical Fire Wall]]).
*[[Fire Ball]]: Generally a solo tool, it can be skipped or left at rank 5 (as a [[Fire Wall]] prerequisite) for more group-focused wizards. If you plan on maxing this skill, you probably shouldn't also max [[Sightrasher]].

===PvE (AGI)===
*STR: 1
*AGI: 50-80*
*VIT: 1+
*INT: 80* or 80+
*DEX: 50-80*
*LUK: 1

Traditionally, Wizards put 99 points into DEX to get the maximum cast time reduction possible, but there is another option: The AGI Wizard. Capitalizing on [[Quagmire]]'s potent 50% DEX debuff, these wizards have an easy time reaching 95% flee even on enemies that others struggle to evade. AGI wizards leverage their evasiveness to make gathering groups of enemies easier and as an alternative means of protection to relying solely on defensive spells. Though still capable of functioning in parties, these wizards are more focused on solo hunting. AGI wizard builds differ depending on whether they intend to use the WELDER card or not.

If using standard equipment, AGI wizards will typically prioritize INT over AGI and DEX as their highest stat. The exact balance between AGI and DEX is dependant on a certain amount of planning, as these wizards aim to reach 95% flee on a given important enemy by a specific level. For example, Fur Seals require 173 FLEE to 95% dodge after being debuffed with [[Quagmire]] 5. Generally speaking, after deciding on their INT and AGI values, DEX is where the remainder of their points go.

AGI Wizards utilizing the WELDER card will typically go no higher than 80 in either AGI, DEX or INT, to capitalize on its bonuses. The WELDER card has 3 effects: It reduces cast time by 10% at DEX <= 80, increases MATK by 10% at INT <= 80, and increases FLEE by 20 at AGI <= 80. Some WELDER wizards opt to go higher than 80 INT. A WELDER-using wizard with 80+25 INT (i.e., with full +INT gear) has ~86% of the MATK that a wizard with 99+21 INT does. Owing to the custom card, this variant of AGI wizard is the most common on PSRO.

===PvE (DEX)===
To no surprise, DEX wizards primarily use equipment that boosts INT, DEX and MATK. Wizards will typically switch out accessories, staves or headgear depending on their needs. For example, a wizard would sport all their DEX gear for low level monster hunting (E.g., Vadons) or static parties where their damage is less relevant. As another example, in a walking party a wizard might want to maximize their damage (i.e., hit the highest INT breakpoint [[Wizard#On INT, MATK Breakpoints & SP Regen]]) and arrange their gear so that they hit their highest min MATK bonus. For solo leveling, a wizard would want to use the stat calculator ([[Wizard#See Also]]) to determine the minimum INT and rank of a given spell like [[Storm Gust]] they need to kill their targets as efficiently as possible and swap around their gear to that end. 

Wizards have a surprising amount of variety when it comes to weapon choices. A Wizardry Staff or the Memory Book Combo (Memory Book + Monocle + Pocket Watch) paired with an Evil Bone Wand are both means of reaching higher MATK values at the cost of survivability. Arc Wand [2] with 2 Drops Cards represents the highest total +stats a 1h staff can provide. Rod [4] carded with Red Ferus or Pitman Cards are niche weapons for boosting [[Meteor Storm]] and [[Heaven's Drive]] damage respectively, as is the Frozen Thunder [1] weapon for [[Lord of Vermilion]] use. The Wing Staff + Eagle Wing [1] combo is another popular option, as its persistent +20% movement speed buff is extremely useful for solo leveling. 

Like most magic casters, any new player or person operating on a budget can still make good use of a wizard as they are far less gear-dependant than physical damage dealers, tanks or mobbers. Evil Bone Wand, Crown/Tiara, Glove [0] and Mage Coat are good first relatively cheap purchases that give a lot of bang for their buck. In terms of larger, but still reasonable investments, a wizard who has access to Creamy and Vitata Carded accessories (easy cards to hunt for a wizard) and the Wing Staff + Eagle Wing [1] combo are empowered when solo leveling.

===PvE (AGI)===
How an AGI wizard equips themself depends on whether they're the regular variant or "WELDER" variant of AGI wiz. Regular AGI wizards use very similar gear to DEX wizards (+INT, +DEX, +MATK), though they may also favour +FLEE cards like FUEL and Whisper. An AGI wizard built around the WELDER card will generally try use their gear to reach the highest INT bonus they can from their tethered place of 80 base INT (E.g., 105 total INT). It should be noted that not all WELDER AGI wizards limit themselves to 80 base int (See [[Wizard#PvE (AGI)]]).

Weapon and budget equipment options for AGI wizards are more or less identical to DEX wizards, though they may also make use of Fur Seal Cards for the bonus to FLEE.

==Wizard Leveling==

''' Recommended Solo Stat Progression '''
* For AGI wizards with WELDER ''and'' flee gear, rush 80 INT -> 80 AGI -> 76 DEX. 
* For non-WELDER AGI wizards or those without equipment, ~80 INT -> 53 DEX will allow you to one cycle Sea Otters (see the leveling guide below) with [[Lord of Vermilion]] and [[Ice Wall]]. Afterwards, AGI wizards will want to pump AGI to have just enough flee for pests at level 90 (195 flee for 95% dodge with [[Quagmire]] 5, 195 flee without it) and at ~100 INT and 65 DEX you can also one cycle Anolians. There are many alternative leveling spots to the above two, but without any plan in mind they can serve as a good landmark for how to allocate your stats as they are probably the most popular for AGI wizards.
* Non-AGI wizards focused on soloing can aim for the above thresholds (~80 INT -> 53 DEX, then ~100 INT 65 DEX) without getting any AGI.

''' Recommended Party Stat Progression '''
* For most parties (especially early on) the most important thing for a wizard is to have a decent cast speed to get off [[Storm Gust]] in time to keep mobs away from the party. 78 base INT is a reasonable ''initial'' stopping point for INT because with [[Blessing]], Job50 bonuses, Clan bonus and an Evil Bone Wand it ends up being 105 INT total (both a min/max MATK bonus).

==Gameplay Tips==
===Protecting Your Party With Storm Gust===
Whether you're in a walking party or a duo, understanding how [[Storm Gust]] works is important for filling your role as a wizard in the vast majority of groups. Each hit of [[Storm Gust]] does a knockback which is '''not''' random. [[Storm Gust]] knocks targets to the northeast, i.e., ''up and to the right'' when the camera is centered. 


<center>[[File:SGInstructional.png|500px]]</center>


What this means in practice is that a [[Storm Gust]] centered on the party will protect them from any monsters entering their immediate vicinity, providing it does not hit monsters to the south of them. This also means that a wizard can more or less predict where their [[Storm Gust]] is going to send monsters it hits, either in a situation where it is cast on top of the party (like in a walking party) or a situation where you'll want to alternate it with another AoE to break monsters out of the ice (like with [[Lord of Vermilion]]).


<center>[[File:SGInstruction1.png|500px]]</center>


In situations where you're casting [[Storm Gust]] for a party, this usually also means the group relies on you to protect them with it. If you get interrupted by a range attack, or a monster spawns on top of you and hits you, this will interrupt your cast and impede your ability to do this. The best solution for these scenario is to have an accessory with a Phen or Bloody Butterfly Card equipped. You don't have to this accessory equipped all the time to protect your cast, you can start your cast without it and then swap to it '''after''' your cast has started. This technique is called '''"Phen switching"'''. It's also a good idea to have a second hotkey with [[Storm Gust]] rank 1 keybound, so you can cast it as fast as possible in an emergency.

===Fire Wall===
====Vertical Fire Wall====
Vertical [[Fire Wall]] is the technique where you cast [[Fire Wall]] adjacent to your character so it casts vertically. This is useful because combined with mobbing and anticipating monster's pathing route, you can have monsters hit all 3 pillars of fire.

<center>[[File:Firewall02.jpg|550px]]</center>
<center>''Cast [[Fire Wall]] on the yellow circle while anticipating for monsters' movements in the red arrow direction.<ref name=":0">http://myrolife.blogspot.com/2016/05/verticle-fire-wall-guide.html</ref>'' </center>


<center>[[File:Firewall03.jpg|500px]]</center>
<center>''Monsters will moving in the red arrow direction, hitting all cells of the [[Fire Wall]].<ref name=":0" />''</center>

For a more in-depth guide on vertical [[Fire Wall]]s, read [http://myrolife.blogspot.com/2016/05/verticle-fire-wall-guide.html Vertical Fire Wall Guide].

====Forced 14-Hit Fire Wall====
This technique makes combined use of careful positioning combined with [[Fire Wall]]'s pushback and [[Ice Wall]] to force even non-[[Undead]] and boss enemies take all 14 hits of each cell of [[Fire Wall]]. There are numerous methods of doing this, but the quickest and most practical is one where the target is attacking the wizard. This technique is more suited for AGI wizards than DEX wizards.

<div style="text-align:center;">[[File:FFW0.gif|300px|]] [[File:FFW1.gif|300px|]]</div>
<center>''A wizard demonstrates the 14-Hit Fire Wall technique''</center>

===Ice Wall===
====Basic Ice Wall Trapping====
Center the camera by double-right-clicking. As the monster is moving from West to East (left to right) or South to North (bottom to top), place an [[Ice Wall]] 1-2 cells in front of them. A second [[Ice Wall]] is then placed immediately adjacent to the 1st [[Ice Wall]], such that the two walls are parallel to one another. The second [[Ice Wall]] is what locks the mobs in place, and also prevents them from being freed if hit by a knockback attack like [[Storm Gust]]. Monsters caught by Ice Wall in this way will become immobilized for as long as the Ice Wall holds. Ice Wall Trapping will not work on monsters moving East to West or North to South, and the wizard is still vulnerable to ranged attacks and attacks by monsters with a 3 cell melee range.

[[Fire Wall]] can be helpful for stacking monsters onto a single cell, allowing for easier [[Ice Wall]] trapping. [[Quagmire]] is also a standard tool when doing wizard wall techniques.

<div style="text-align:center;">[[File:Icewall-trapping.gif|428px|Icewall-trapping.gif]] [[File:Ice Trapping Demonstration0.gif|Ice Trapping Demonstration0.gif]] </div>

'''Backup'''

In the event that one or more monsters slips out of your [[Ice Wall]] trap because they were too far out of the group or timing was a little off, you can put down a second set of [[Ice Wall]] rows to trap them. Keep in mind the "West to East or South to North" rule previously mentioned still applies.

<div style="text-align:center;">[[File:IWTBackup0.gif|375px|IWTBackup0.gif]] </div>

====Bangman's Z Ice Prison====
Normally, a monster that isn't immune to [[Freeze]] hit by [[Storm Gust]] will be frozen after being struck by it three times. This is very useful for controlling monsters, but limits [[Storm Gust]]'s potential damage. There are techniques that wizards can employ using [[Sight Blaster]], [[Fire Pillar]] and [[Ice Wall]] to bypass this limitation, and leverage the (almost) full power of [[Storm Gust]] hitting monsters 9 times instead of 3. The safest and most consistent method of doing this is with "Bangman's Z Ice Prison" 

{| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"
|+ class="nowrap" | Z Ice Prison Guide
|


<center>'''Z Ice Prison can be broken down into 11 steps:'''</center>

1. Mobs are tightly stacked (usually with [[Quagmire]] and vertical [[Fire Wall]]) and then an [[Ice Wall]] is placed 2 cells left and 1 cell up from your character.

[[File:ZPrisonInfographic1.png|275px|ZPrisonInfographic1.png|]]

2. The second [[Ice Wall]] is placed 2 cells right and 1 cell up from your character.

[[File:ZPrisonInfographic2.png|275px|ZPrisonInfographic2.png|]]

3. The third [[Ice Wall]] is placed 2 cells to the right of the 2nd [[Ice Wall]] (i.e., 4 cells right, 1 cell up from your character). This [[Ice Wall]] must be cast before the mobs move past your second 2nd [[Ice Wall]], and when done correctly will cause them to "bounce" off of it.

[[File:ZPrisonInfographic3.png|275px|ZPrisonInfographic3.png|]]

4. The fourth [[Ice Wall]] is placed 1 cell right and 4 cells up from your character (right next to the end point of the 1st [[Ice Wall]])

[[File:ZPrisonInfographic4.png|275px|ZPrisonInfographic4.png|]]

5. A [[Fire Pillar]] is placed 2 cells down from your character.

[[File:ZPrisonInfographic5.png|275px|ZPrisonInfographic5.png|]]

6. A second [[Fire Pillar]] is placed 2 cells left, 2 cells down from the 1st [[Fire Pillar]] (i.e., 3 cells left and 4 cells down from your character)

[[File:ZPrisonInfographic6.png|275px|ZPrisonInfographic6.png|]]

7. The wizard then moves 1 cell down and 1 cell to the left of the 2nd [[Fire Pillar]].

[[File:ZPrisonInfographic7.png|275px|ZPrisonInfographic7.png|]]

8. The wizard casts [[Sight Blaster]], knocking [[Fire Pillar]] #2 up and to the right.

[[File:ZPrisonInfographic8.png|275px|ZPrisonInfographic8.png|]]

9. The wizard casts [[Storm Gust]] on the enemy group.

[[File:ZPrisonInfographic9.png|275px|ZPrisonInfographic9.png|]]

10. As soon as the third [[Storm Gust]] wave hits the group (and freezes them), the wizard moves 2 cells up and 2 cells right, knocking [[Fire Pillar]] #1 into the group of enemies (breaking them enemies out of their ice).

[[File:ZPrisonInfographic10.png|275px|ZPrisonInfographic10.png|]]

11. The wizard then waits for the '''second''' freeze from [[Storm Gust]] after 3 more hits and then moves 1 cell up and 1 cell right, knocking [[Fire Pillar]] #2 into the group of enemies (once more breaking their ice).

===="6 Hit SG"====
A more lightweight version of the Left-to-Right Trap, this technique uses basic [[Ice Wall]] trapping and [[Sight Blaster]] to break the first freeze on enemies hit by [[Storm Gust]], hitting them 6 times with the spell instead of 3. 

Enemies are first trapped using basic [[Ice Wall]] trapping. [[Sight Blaster]] is then cast, followed by [[Storm Gust]]. Once the enemies are frozen by the third hit of [[Storm Gust]], the wizard walks alongside the [[Ice Wall]] to break the mob's ice with [[Sight Blaster]].

<div style="text-align:center;">[[File:6HitSG0.gif|6HitSG0.gif|]] [[File:6HitSG1.gif|6HitSG1.gif|]]</div>

===On INT, MATK Breakpoints & SP Regen===
MATK before gear and other modifiers is calculated by this formula: Min MATK = (INT + [INT / 7]^2) ~ Max MATK = (INT + [INT / 5]^2), where INT is rounded down each time.

This MATK is then modified by gear effects like +15% from most Staves and set bonuses like Survivor's and Pocket Watch combo.

So INT scales MATK and thus damage quadratically in increments of 5 and 7. It also increases Max SP and SP Regen by 1% of Base SP every INT and 1 point per tick every 6 INT respectively. The increased Max SP also increases SP Regen by 1 for every 100 total Max SP. Once you reach 120 INT there is a further SP Regen increase by 1 point every 2 INT above 112 INT, so 4 right away and 1 every 2 INT from then on. Since SP Regen is a major limiting factor for Wizards, considerations of SP Regen become just as, if not more important than DPS. This is why most Wizards will use high INT gear even in situations where DEX would theoretically provide slightly better DPS.

Some examples of INT breakpoints that wizards typically aim for are 105, 120 and 126 (with or without [[Blessing]]), and 130 and 135 (with [[Blessing]]).

===On DEX & Instant Cast===
The effect of DEX on cast time is expressed by this formula: Cast Time Multiplier = 1 - (DEX / 150), this means each DEX reduces it by 1/150 and at 150 DEX cast time becomes instant. Since every point of DEX reduces cast time by a flat amount, at high DEX each point reduces the remaining cast time by a relatively larger amount. The first DEX reduces cast time by 1/150 both in absolute, as well as relative terms. But the 150th DEX still reduces the overall cast time by 1/150, however relative to the cast time at 149 DEX it's a 100% reduction (down do 0). The next point of DEX is always better than the last (its effect scales non-linearly) and this is the reason DEX gear can outscale INT gear in some circumstances (with good Bragi and while using Spells that can stack), despite INT increasing MATK quadratically. The maximum attainable DEX for Wizards is in the high 130s (137 at the time of this writing).

In Payon Stories, Wizards can't reach instant cast. There are no stat foods to facilitate this and no custom gear lets you reach 150 DEX either.

=== On After Cast Delay (ACD) ===
Most Wizard skills have very high ACD. As one example, the ACD of [[Storm Gust]] (SG) is so high the spell fully expires before you can start casting another one. In a group situation, even with extremely high DEX it's not possible to get full SG coverage with one Wizard alone. Two Wizards could alternate casts, but there is one skill that makes a single Wizard better than two combined. 

[[Bard]]'s [[A Poem of Bragi]] is the only way currently to reduce cast delay. For a [[Bard]] with at least 150 DEX and 100 INT it reduces cast time by more than half (55%) and cuts cast delay down by a whopping 90%. Even low DEX Wizards can lock down an area with constantly active SG and break the frozen enemies themselves with Lord of Vermillion (LoV) casts in between SG casts. A single high level Wizard with an appropriately built [[Bard]] providing Bragi can throw out multiple casts of other skills in between SG casts and keep a party completely untouchable due to the sheer volume of Crowd Control (CC) and Damage output, especially if the [[Bard]] adds Arrow Showers to keep stragglers in the correct area of SG. With high enough INT the ACD of most skills will be shorter than the animation of the cast itself. This is generally called "Animation Capping" and the only way to further increase your cast speed is to either increase Attack Speed (with Berserk Potions for example), or cancel the animation by moving at the exact right moment ("Dancing").

Due to the effect of Bragi alone, Wizards are capable of dealing much greater DPS in parties than solo and are part of the core trio (Wiz/Bard/Priest) of many popular endgame party setups.
